## Definition

All vector and matrix indices below start at $0$. A rectangular Toeplitz matrix $T\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$, where $m,n\ge1$, is specified by lags $t_r\in\mathbb C$ for $-(n-1)\le r\le m-1$ and has entries
$$T_{ij}:=t_{i-j}\qquad(0\le i<m,\ 0\le j<n).$$
For a square matrix $T\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, Hermitian Toeplitz means $t_{-r}=\overline{t_r}$ for $0\le r<n$. It is positive definite when $x^*Tx>0$ for every nonzero $x\in\mathbb C^n$, where $x^*:=\overline{x}^{\,T}$ and the product is the matrix product of [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]].

For $N\ge1$, a vector $c=(c_0,\ldots,c_{N-1})^T\in\mathbb C^N$ generates the circulant matrix
$$C(c)_{ij}:=c_{(i-j)\bmod N}\qquad(0\le i,j<N).$$
For $n\ge1$ and $0\le j<n$, let $e_j\in\mathbb C^n$ be the coordinate vector with $(e_j)_i=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise. For $a\in\mathbb C^n$, $J_na$ is the reversed vector, $(J_na)_i=a_{n-1-i}$; $J_0$ is the unique map on the empty vector. The lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $L(a)\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with $L(a)_{ij}=a_{i-j}$ when $i\ge j$, and $0$ otherwise. The canonical unitary DFT is the map $\mathcal F_N$ of [[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]; the unnormalised DFT used for operation counts is $D_N:=\sqrt N\,\mathcal F_N$.

These conventions specify matrix orientation, conjugation, normalization, and boundary indexing; in particular, circulant eigenvalues below use the negative-sign canonical DFT.

## Definition

Fix gravity $g>0$ and a stationary bed $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$. A shallow-water state is a pair $U=(h,m)$ with depth $h\ge0$ and momentum $m\in\mathbb R$. Its admissible wet/dry state set is
$$K=\{(h,m):h>0,\ m\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.$$
For $U\in K$, define velocity by $u=m/h$ when $h>0$ and $u=0$ when $h=0$. Thus a dry state has both $h=0$ and $m=0$. Define the free surface by $\eta=h+b$ and the physical flux by
$$F(U)=\begin{cases}(m,\ m^2/h+gh^2/2),&h>0,\\(0,0),&U=(0,0).\end{cases}$$
For a continuously differentiable bed, the one-dimensional shallow-water balance law is
$$U_t+\partial_xF(U)=(0,-gh\,b_x).$$
The source is evaluated as zero at a dry state.

A discrete lake-at-rest profile with level $\eta_0$ has $m_i=0$ and $h_i+b_i=\eta_0$ in every wet cell; cells with $h_i=0$ are dry and satisfy $b_i\ge\eta_0$.

## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$. An **admissible smoothing kernel** is a radial function $W\in C_c^2(\mathbb R^d,[0,\infty))$, supported in the closed Euclidean ball $\overline B(0,R)$ of some radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}W(z)\,dz=1$. Here radial means $W(z)=w(|z|)$ for some function $w:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, and $C_c^2$ means twice continuously differentiable with compact support. All vector norms are the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and $\|D^2W\|_\infty$ uses the induced operator norm. Throughout this pair, $L^\infty$ norms are suprema of Euclidean norms, and norms of multilinear derivatives are the induced operator norms. Compactly supported integrals use [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]], where $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of the set on which $f$ is nonzero.

For $\varepsilon>0$ define the scaled kernel $W_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-d}W(z/\varepsilon)$. Write $M_0=\|W\|_\infty$, $M_1=\|\nabla W\|_\infty$, $M_2=\|D^2W\|_\infty$, $m_2=\int |z|^2W(z)\,dz$, and $m_3=\int |z|^3|\nabla W(z)|\,dz$. The norm functions and moment integrands are continuous with compact support. They are bounded and Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], so these constants are finite.

For continuous $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, define the full-space smoother and its kernel-gradient operator by
$$S_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x-z)W_\varepsilon(z)\,dz,\qquad D_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(y)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy.$$
For each fixed $x$, both scalar integrands and every component of the vector integrand are continuous and compactly supported, hence Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. Thus the displayed integrals exist as compactly supported Riemann integrals; the vector integral defining $D_\varepsilon f$ is taken componentwise.

This page fixes $\varepsilon$ in the finite-particle system. Limits $\varepsilon\to0$ are used only in the stated kernel-bias and joint-refinement results.

An **admissible smoothing kernel** is a radial function $W\in C_c^2(\mathbb R^d,[0,\infty))$, supported in the closed Euclidean ball $\overline B(0,R)$ of some radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}W(z)\,dz=1$. Here radial means $W(z)=w(|z|)$ for some function $w:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, and $C_c^2$ means twice continuously differentiable with compact support. All vector norms are the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and $\|D^2W\|_\infty$ uses the induced operator norm. Throughout this pair, $L^\infty$ norms are suprema of Euclidean norms, and norms of multilinear derivatives are the induced operator norms. Compactly supported integrals use [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]], where $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of the set on which $f$ is nonzero.

For $\varepsilon>0$ define the scaled kernel $W_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-d}W(z/\varepsilon)$. Write $M_0=\|W\|_\infty$, $M_1=\|\nabla W\|_\infty$, $M_2=\|D^2W\|_\infty$, $m_2=\int |z|^2W(z)\,dz$, and $m_3=\int |z|^3|\nabla W(z)|\,dz$. The norm functions and moment integrands are continuous with compact support. They are bounded and Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], so these constants are finite.

For continuous $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, define the full-space smoother and its kernel-gradient operator by
$$S_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x-z)W_\varepsilon(z)\,dz,\qquad D_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(y)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy.$$
For each fixed $x$, both scalar integrands and every component of the vector integrand are continuous and compactly supported, hence Riemann integrable on a bounding Jordan box by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. Thus the displayed integrals exist as compactly supported Riemann integrals; the vector integral defining $D_\varepsilon f$ is taken componentwise.

This page fixes $\varepsilon$ in the finite-particle system. Limits $\varepsilon\to0$ are used only in the stated kernel-bias and joint-refinement results.

## Definition

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

## Statement

Let $A:V\to V'$ be symmetric positive definite on a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let $L:V\to U$, $T:U\to V$ satisfy $LT=I_U$. Every eigenvalue of

$$G=(LA^{-1}L^T)(T^TAT)$$

lies in $[1,\|TL\|_A^2]$, where $\|Q\|_A:=\sup_{v\ne0}\sqrt{\langle A Qv,Qv\rangle/\langle Av,v\rangle}$. When $V=\{0\}$, set $\|Q\|_A=0$ for its unique endomorphism. In that case $LT=I_U$ forces $U=\{0\}$, the spectrum of $G$ is empty, and the eigenvalue assertion is vacuous.

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set,
$0<r<1$, and let $q$ be a measurable real function on $U$. Define
$$[q]_{H^r(U)}^2:=\int_U\int_U\frac{|q(x)-q(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2r}}\,dx\,dy,$$
with the diagonal integrand set to zero, and
$H^r(U):=\{q\in L^2(U):[q]_{H^r(U)}<\infty\}$, using almost-everywhere
classes and norm $\|q\|_{H^r(U)}^2:=\|q\|_{L^2(U)}^2+[q]_{H^r(U)}^2$.
For $u\in H^1(U)$, write $u\in H^{1+r}(U)$ when each weak derivative
$\partial_j u$ belongs to $H^r(U)$, and define
$$|u|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2:=\sum_{j=1}^d[\partial_j u]_{H^r(U)}^2.$$
For vector fields, use the sum of the componentwise squared $H^r$ norms.
Use these definitions on each cell $K$ and on the full domain $\Omega$, with
$\|u\|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2:=\|u\|_{H^1(U)}^2+|u|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2$. At $r=1$,
set $H^1(U)=W^{1,2}(U)$, interpret $[q]_{H^1(U)}^2:=\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(U)}^2$,
and set $H^{1+r}(U)=W^{2,2}(U)$ with the ordinary integer-order norm and
membership of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Thus
$|u|_{H^2(U)}^2=\sum_{j,k}\|\partial_k\partial_j u\|_{L^2(U)}^2$. The local
seminorm is the restriction of the Slobodeckij convention in
[[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] to $U\times U$.

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice for the $H_0^1$ convention of [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix a finite conforming triangular mesh $\mathcal T$. For each interior vertex $z$, choose the incident triangle with least fixed mesh index and denote it $K_z$. On the reference triangle $\widehat K$, let $\widehat\lambda_1,\widehat\lambda_2,\widehat\lambda_3$ be its barycentric coordinates. The Gram matrix $G_{ij}=\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_i\widehat\lambda_j$ is positive definite because $\int_{\widehat K}p^2>0$ for every nonzero $p\in P_1(\widehat K)$. Thus there are unique dual affine polynomials $\widehat\psi_i\in P_1(\widehat K)$ with $\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_j\widehat\psi_i=\delta_{ij}$. Pull them to $K_z$ by the affine map using the normalized measure so $\int_{K_z}\varphi_y\psi_{z,K_z}=\delta_{zy}$ for its three local nodal hats.

For $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ set $c_z(v)=\int_{K_z}v\psi_{z,K_z}$ at interior vertices and $c_z(v)=0$ at boundary vertices. Define
$$I_{\mathcal T}v=\sum_{z\ {\rm interior}}c_z(v)\varphi_z,$$
where $\varphi_z$ is the continuous piecewise-affine nodal hat. The sum is finite and belongs to the conforming zero-boundary P1 space. This is a moment quasi-interpolant; it is not a point-evaluation operator on arbitrary Sobolev classes.

## Definition

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Use the unit sphere $S^2$ and its polar surface measure $d\sigma$ from [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. For each integer $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the complex vector space of restrictions to $S^2$ of homogeneous degree-$\ell$ polynomials $P$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the Euclidean harmonic equation $\Delta P=0$. In polar coordinates $x=r\omega$, define $\Delta_{S^2}$ by
$$\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}=\partial_r^2+\frac2r\partial_r+\frac1{r^2}\Delta_{S^2},$$
equivalently $\Delta_{S^2}=\frac1{\sin\theta}\partial_\theta(\sin\theta\partial_\theta)+\frac1{\sin^2\theta}\partial_\phi^2$ away from the poles. Thus if $Y\in\mathcal H_\ell$ is the restriction of $P$, then $\Delta_{S^2}Y=-\ell(\ell+1)Y$.

For $\ell\ge0$, define the normalized zonal polynomial $P_\ell(t)$ to be the degree-$\ell$ polynomial satisfying
$$ (1-t^2)P_\ell''(t)-2tP_\ell'(t)+\ell(\ell+1)P_\ell(t)=0,\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$
The later harmonic-basis lemma proves existence and uniqueness of this normalized polynomial and identifies it with the usual Legendre convention.

The term **partial wave of degree $\ell$** means the $\mathcal H_\ell$ component of an angular expansion in $L^2(S^2,d\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Completeness, orthogonality, finite dimension, and the evaluation bound for these components are established in [[lem-spherical-harmonics-form-complete-basis-and-addition-formula]].

For a radial field $u(r,\omega)$, its degree-$\ell$ component is written $u_\ell(r,\omega)\in\mathcal H_\ell$; any orthonormal basis within this finite-dimensional space gives the equivalent scalar mode equations. The definition does not select such a basis globally.

## Definition

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$. Let $\mathbb T^d=[0,1)^d$ be the chosen representatives for period-one coordinates; all coordinates in a type-1 or type-2 transform are interpreted modulo integer shifts. Here $\pi$ is the real constant defined in [[def-real-elementary-functions-and-domains]]. For $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, write $k\cdot x=\sum_{r=1}^d k_rx_r$. Let $N,J\ge0$ be finite integers, let $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}\in\mathbb T^d$, let $c=(c_j)_{j<N}\in\mathbb C^N$, and choose integers $K_r\ge0$. The rectangular mode set is

$$\mathcal K=\prod_{r=1}^d\{-K_r,-K_r+1,\ldots,K_r\}.$$

The **type-1 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** maps source coefficients to integer-mode samples:

$$F_k=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j},\qquad k\in\mathcal K.$$

The **type-2 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** maps a coefficient array $(f_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}$ to values at the same point list:

$$g_j=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}f_k e^{+2\pi i k\cdot x_j},\qquad 0\le j<N.$$

For the type-1 matrix $A=(e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x_j})_{k\in\mathcal K,\,j<N}$, define its conjugate transpose by $(A^*)_{jk}=\overline{A_{kj}}$. Use the finite counting inner products from [[def-nufft-finite-array-norms]]; the type-2 matrix is $A^*$ as proved below.

The **type-3 nonuniform discrete Fourier transform** takes a finite source list $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}\in\mathbb R^d$, coefficients $c_j\in\mathbb C$, and a separately specified finite frequency list $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_{J-1}\in\mathbb R^d$, and returns

$$G_\ell=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}c_j e^{-2\pi i \xi_\ell\cdot x_j},\qquad 0\le\ell<J.$$

Type 3 has no integer-mode restriction or implicit coordinate wrapping. No frequency normalization, axis scaling, or frequency-space product is implicit; any such scaling is separate input data whose cost must be analyzed separately. Each displayed map is a finite sum of defined complex exponentials; the zero-source case has the empty-sum value zero and the zero-output case returns the empty array. No fast algorithm or complexity claim for type 3 is part of this definition.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $p_0,\ldots,p_d,q\in\mathbb D^d$, and let their dyadic weights be $w_0,\ldots,w_d,w_q$ (zero when absent). Assume $p_0,\ldots,p_d$ are affinely independent. If $c\in\mathbb R^d$ and $R\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$$\|p_i-c\|^2-w_i=R\qquad(0\le i\le d),$$
define the power difference
$$\Delta(q)=\|q-c\|^2-w_q-R.$$
Let $O_d$ be the determinant of the rows $(p_i,1)$ for $i=0,\ldots,d$, and let $P_d$ be the determinant of the $d+2$ rows $(p_i,\|p_i\|^2-w_i,1)$, including the query row $(q,\|q\|^2-w_q,1)$. Then
$$P_d=-O_d\Delta(q),\qquad O_dP_d=-O_d^2\Delta(q).$$
Thus the sign of $O_dP_d$ is positive, zero or negative exactly when $q$ is respectively inside, on or outside the power sphere. When all weights are zero, this is the ordinary circumsphere convention.

## Statement

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb K^n$ have dimension $d\ge1$, where
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. For any orthonormal basis matrix
$Q\in\mathbb K^{n\times d}$, let $\ell_i=\|e_i^*Q\|_2^2$. Then
these values are independent of the chosen orthonormal basis, satisfy
$0\le\ell_i\le1$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\ell_i=d$, and $\ell_i=0$
exactly when the $i$-th row of $Q$ is zero.

## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_k$ for
$0\le k\le T$, and positive observation dimensions $p_k$ for
$1\le k\le T$. Inputs are real finite matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times
d_{k-1}}$, $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, observation vectors
$y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$, and an initial mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$.
For each covariance supply a rectangular real factor
$$L_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times r_0},\qquad L_{Q,k}\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times r_{Q,k}},\qquad L_{R,k}\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times r_{R,k}},$$
where each column count is any finite nonnegative integer. The represented
covariances are $P_0=L_0L_0^T$, $Q_k=L_{Q,k}L_{Q,k}^T$, and
$R_k=L_{R,k}L_{R,k}^T$. Thus zero columns and rank-deficient factors are
allowed. The admissible statistical inputs are those of
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] for which
the canonical innovation $S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k$ is positive definite at each
step. The [[def-axiom-of-choice]] assumption is inherited only for the
interpretation as a posterior; the finite matrix procedure itself uses no
probability-space choice.

Choose a unit roundoff $u$ in the no-underflow operationwise model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Every matrix or vector product below is evaluated as left-to-right dot
products. A nonzero nonnormal intermediate, nonfinite result, zero innovation
diagonal, or failed factorization returns a status and the first failing step;
it is not coerced into a covariance
estimate. Each arithmetic and factorization failure has a declared return;
there is no iterative convergence loop or unbounded refinement search.

The QR operation used below is the following unpivoted reduced procedure on
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n\ge1$. Initialize a working array
$R^{(0)}=A$ and an empty ordered reflector list. For $j=1,\ldots,n$, take
$x=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j}$ and $B=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j+1:n}$, call
[[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] on $(x,B)$,
and, on success, replace the active block by its returned $C_+$. If the call
fails, return its first status and step. Store the exact orthogonal reflector
represented by the returned record, or the identity for its identity branch.
After $n$ successful steps, return the computed upper-triangular block
$R=R^{(n)}_{1:n,1:n}$ and the ordered reflector list representing the exact
product $Q_{\rm full}$ whose first $n$ columns are the reduced $Q$ factor.
Do not materialize a rounded dense $Q$. The conventions are those of
[[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]].

Initialize $m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $L_{0|0}=L_0$. At step $k$, perform the
following operations in order.

1. Compute the rounded mean prediction $\widehat m_{k|k-1}
=\operatorname{fl}(F_k\widehat m_{k-1|k-1})$. Form the rounded factor product
$\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}(F_kL_{k-1|k-1})$. Concatenate
$\widehat G_k=[\widehat X_k\;L_{Q,k}]$ and append zero columns until its
column count is $q_k=\max(d_k,r_{k-1|k-1}+r_{Q,k})$. Apply the above
reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat G_k^T\in\mathbb R^{q_k\times d_k}$. On success let $R_k^{p}$ be
its reduced upper factor and set $L_{k|k-1}= (R_k^{p})^T$. No diagonal
positivity or full-rank condition is imposed on this prediction factor.

2. Compute $\widehat v_k=\operatorname{fl}
(y_k-\operatorname{fl}(H_k\widehat m_{k|k-1}))$. Pad $L_{R,k}$ with zero
columns to $\bar r_k=\max(p_k,r_{R,k})$ columns. Compute
$\widehat Y_k=\operatorname{fl}(H_kL_{k|k-1})$ and form the block prearray
$$\widehat Z_k= \begin{bmatrix} L_{R,k}^{\mathrm{pad}} & \widehat Y_k\\ 0 & L_{k|k-1} \end{bmatrix}.$$
Apply the above reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat Z_k^T\in\mathbb R^{(\bar r_k+d_k)\times(p_k+d_k)}$. Its row
count is at least its column count: the prediction step gives
$L_{k|k-1}\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times d_k}$, and $\bar r_k\ge p_k$. On success
transpose its reduced upper factor and partition the resulting lower factor as
$$\widehat L_k=\begin{bmatrix}\widehat L_{11,k}&0\\ \widehat L_{21,k}&\widehat L_{22,k}\end{bmatrix},$$
with block sizes $p_k$ and $d_k$. If any diagonal entry of $\widehat
L_{11,k}$ is zero, return `innovation-factorization-failure`. Otherwise,
for each $i=1,\ldots,p_k$, multiply column $i$ of the whole factor
$\widehat L_k$ by the sign of its diagonal entry. These exact sign changes
make $\widehat L_{11,k}$ have positive diagonal and preserve
$\widehat L_k\widehat L_k^T$ and its lower block structure. Use the resulting
factor blocks below. No invertibility or positive diagonal is required of
$\widehat L_{22,k}$.

3. Solve $\widehat L_{11,k}\widehat z_k=\widehat v_k$ by forward
substitution in the order of
[[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]]. Set
$$\widehat m_{k|k}=\operatorname{fl} (\widehat m_{k|k-1}+\widehat L_{21,k}\widehat z_k),\qquad L_{k|k}=\widehat L_{22,k}.$$
Do not form a covariance downdate or an explicit matrix inverse. The
factor-defined covariance $L_{k|k}L_{k|k}^T$ is positive semidefinite as an
exact product of the returned entries; no claim is made that a separately
rounded materialization of that product remains positive semidefinite.

4. If any arithmetic operation or QR call returns a failure status, return the
first such failure and its step; if the leading innovation block has a zero
diagonal, return innovation-factorization-failure. Otherwise the finite loop
returns the predicted and updated mean/factor arrays with success. The success
status records arithmetic and factorization completion only.

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the output is $(m_0,L_0)$ with no update
status. In exact arithmetic, the result implements the covariance and mean map of
[[alg-kalman-filter]]. The prediction factor identity is supplied by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-prediction-factor-identity]], and the measurement
block identity by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-measurement-block-factor-identity]]. Under the
inherited AC assumption
its statistical interpretation is the one in
[[thm-kalman-filter-is-exact-posterior]]. The nearby covariance supplied by
an unstructured QR backward error may introduce cross-correlations between
model blocks. Therefore no backward-stability claim within the original
independent-noise state-space model, and no uniform-in-time accuracy or
stability claim, is part of this procedure.

## Definition

Let $\ell\ge0$ be an integer and $z>0$ real. Put
$$c_\ell=(2\ell+1)!!=\prod_{r=0}^{\ell}(2r+1),\qquad d_\ell=(2\ell-1)!!=\prod_{r=1}^{\ell}(2r-1),$$
where the second product is empty and equals $1$ when $\ell=0$. Using the outgoing convention of [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]], define
$$J_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=c_\ell z^{-\ell}j_\ell(z),\qquad D J_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=c_\ell z^{-\ell}j_\ell'(z),$$
$$H_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}e^{-iz}h_\ell^{(1)}(z),\qquad D H_\ell^{\rm sc}(z)=d_\ell^{-1}z^{\ell+1}e^{-iz}(h_\ell^{(1)})'(z).$$
The symbols $D J_\ell^{\rm sc}$ and $D H_\ell^{\rm sc}$ mean the scaled derivatives of the original functions, not derivatives of the scaled functions. The available targets are $j_\ell$, $j_\ell'$, $h_\ell^{(1)}$, $(h_\ell^{(1)})'$, and these four scaled quantities; every derivative is with respect to $z$.

An input is either (i) a closed dyadic interval $I=[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)$, requesting an enclosure of the whole target image on $I$, or (ii) a positive real $z$ supplied by an interface that, on each integer request $n\ge1$, terminates and returns a closed dyadic interval $I_n$ containing $z$ with width at most $2^{-n}$. The intervals need not be nested. This is a representation hypothesis on a supplied input, not a claim that every positive real has such a representation. An exact positive dyadic point is the constant-interface case $I_n=[z,z]$. A represented point need not be dyadic: arguments such as $kR$ or $\sqrt{k^2+V_0}R$ are admitted when a caller constructs a terminating interface by rigorous interval propagation from represented parameters. Each returned box must contain the exact composed argument; a midpoint or approximate point alone is not an admissible interface. The caller's construction must retain positivity and prove termination of every requested refinement.

For each target, outputs and optional relative tests use [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]: a real enclosure is an interval, a complex enclosure is a rectangle, and its radius is half its length or half its Euclidean diagonal, respectively. Each target has an exact positive rational absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a$; an exact positive rational relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r$ may also be requested. ## Definition

Fix $p\ge0$, source labels $J$ with positions $y_j\in\mathbb R^3$ and charges $q_j\in\mathbb C$, a center $c$, and a radius $a\ge0$ with $|y_j-c|\le a$. For each $0\le\ell\le p$, supply an orthonormal basis $\{Y_{\ell m}:-\ell\le m\le\ell\}$ of $\mathcal H_\ell$ from [[def-three-dimensional-spherical-harmonic-space]]; its existence and dimension are given by [[lem-three-dimensional-laplace-spherical-harmonic-addition-theorem]]. Form moments
$$M_{\ell m}=\sum_{j\in J}q_j\overline{H_{\ell m}(y_j-c)}.$$
For every target $x$ with $r=|x-c|>a$, evaluate the truncated single-cluster multipole field
$$\widetilde U_p(x)=4\pi\sum_{\ell=0}^p\frac{1}{2\ell+1}\frac{1}{r^{\ell+1}}\sum_{m=-\ell}^{\ell}M_{\ell m}Y_{\ell m}\!\left(\frac{x-c}{r}\right).$$
The output is an approximation to $U(x)=\sum_{j\in J}q_j/|x-y_j|$. This is the source-cluster-to-target evaluator only; it makes no 3D tree-translation or global all-target complexity claim.

For the arithmetic count, store each basis polynomial by its monomial coefficient array. Basis setup is done once for the chosen $p$. To evaluate the displayed formula directly, evaluate every basis polynomial by summing its monomials at each source and target point, then accumulate the moments and target sums. This convention makes the basis-evaluation work explicit rather than treating each special-function evaluation as free.

## Statement

Fix a finite horizon $T$ and let $(m_{k|k},P_{k|k})$ and
$(m_k^-,P_k^-)$ be the exact real-arithmetic prediction and update recursions
of [[alg-kalman-filter]]. Let
$$S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k,\qquad B_k=P_k^-H_k^T,\qquad v_k=y_k-H_km_k^-.$$
Suppose each innovation has a certified lower bound
$$x^TS_kx\ge\mu_k\|x\|_2^2\quad(x\in\mathbb R^{p_k}),\qquad \mu_k>0.$$
Let the procedure [[alg-finite-budget-square-root-kalman-filter]] output represented covariances
$\widehat P_{k|k}=\widehat L_{k|k}\widehat L_{k|k}^T$ and means
$\widehat m_{k|k}$. At step $k$, assume certified local bounds
$$\begin{aligned} &\|\widehat P_k^--(F_k\widehat P_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k)\|_2\le e_k^P,\\ &\|\widehat J_k-J_k(\widehat P_k^-)\|_2\le e_k^J,\\ &\|\widehat m_k^--F_k\widehat m_{k-1|k-1}\|_2\le e_k^m,\\ &\|\widehat v_k-(y_k-H_k\widehat m_k^-)\|_2\le e_k^v,\\ &\|\widehat L_{11,k}\widehat z_k-\widehat v_k\|_2\le\rho_k,\\ &\|\widehat m_{k|k}-(\widehat m_k^-+\widehat L_{21,k}\widehat z_k)\|_2\le e_k^u, \end{aligned}$$
where
$$J_k(P)=\begin{bmatrix}H_kPH_k^T+R_k&H_kP\\PH_k^T&P\end{bmatrix}$$
and $\widehat J_k=\widehat L_k\widehat L_k^T$ is the joint covariance
represented by the measurement QR blocks. Let $f_k\ge\|F_k\|_2$,
$h_k\ge\|H_k\|_2$, $b_k\ge\|B_k\|_2$, and
$r_k\ge\|v_k\|_2$ be certified finite upper bounds. Choose
$\Delta_0\ge\|\widehat m_{0|0}-m_0\|_2+
\|\widehat P_{0|0}-P_0\|_2$.

Define recursively
$$c_k^H=1+h_k^2,\qquad \varepsilon_k=c_k^H(f_k^2\Delta_{k-1}+e_k^P)+e_k^J.$$
If $\varepsilon_k\le\mu_k/2$, put
$$K_k^\#=1+2b_k/\mu_k,\qquad C_k^K=\frac2{\mu_k}\left(1+\frac{b_k}{\mu_k}\right),\qquad C_k^P=2+\frac{4b_k}{\mu_k}+2\left(\frac{b_k}{\mu_k}\right)^2,$$
$$A_k=(1+h_kK_k^\#)f_k+ (C_k^Kr_k+C_k^P)c_k^Hf_k^2,$$
$$\eta_k=(1+h_kK_k^\#)e_k^m+ (C_k^Kr_k+C_k^P)(c_k^He_k^P+e_k^J)+ K_k^\#(e_k^v+\rho_k)+e_k^u, \qquad \Delta_k=A_k\Delta_{k-1}+\eta_k.$$
Then each $\widehat S_k$ is positive definite, the factor update is
defined, and, with $z_k^*=\widehat L_{11,k}^{-1}\widehat v_k$,
$$\|\widehat z_k-z_k^*\|_2\le \frac{\rho_k}{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat L_{11,k})} \le\sqrt{\frac2{\mu_k}}\,\rho_k,$$
where $\sigma_{\min}(T)=\min_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Tx\|_2$. Also
$$\|\widehat m_{T|T}-m_{T|T}\|_2+ \|\widehat P_{T|T}-P_{T|T}\|_2\le\Delta_T.$$
Equivalently,
$$\Delta_T=\left(\prod_{k=1}^T A_k\right)\Delta_0+ \sum_{j=1}^T\left(\prod_{k=j+1}^T A_k\right)\eta_j,$$
where an empty product is $1$. The bound is finite-horizon and explicitly
conditioned on the innovation margins and data scales. It implies no
uniform-in-time stability or accuracy claim.

## Statement

For $z\ne0$, the functions in [[def-integer-order-bessel-series]] satisfy

$$z^2J_n''+zJ_n'+(z^2-n^2)J_n=0, \qquad z^2I_n''+zI_n'-(z^2+n^2)I_n=0.$$

For real or complex $z\ne0$ and integer $n\ge1$, they also satisfy

$$J_{n-1}(z)+J_{n+1}(z)=\frac{2n}{z}J_n(z), \qquad I_{n-1}(z)-I_{n+1}(z)=\frac{2n}{z}I_n(z).$$

In addition, $J_0'(z)=-J_1(z)$.

At $z=0$, the series limits are $J_0(0)=I_0(0)=1$ and
$J_n(0)=I_n(0)=0$ for $n\ge1$.

## Statement

Let $\alpha<2$ and let $q:T\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. On $T\setminus\{(0,0)\}$ put $f(x,y)=\|(x,y)\|_2^{-\alpha}q(x,y)$, where $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm. The improper integral over $T$ is absolutely convergent and
$$\int_T f(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\int_0^1\int_0^1 r^{1-\alpha}G(r,s)\,ds\,dr, \qquad G(r,s)=(1+s^2)^{-\alpha/2}q(r,rs).$$
In particular, the transformed radial weight $r^{1-\alpha}$ is integrable at zero because $1-\alpha>-1$.

## Statement

Let $m\in\mathbb N_0$, $s=m+\tfrac12$, and $T>\max\{s-1,0\}$. Then
$$F_m(T)=\frac{\Gamma(s)-R_s(T)}{2T^s},\qquad R_s(T)=\int_T^\infty u^{s-1}e^{-u}\,du,$$

$$\left[\frac{\Gamma(s)}{2T^s}-\frac{T^{s-1}e^{-T}}{2T^s(1-\max\{s-1,0\}/T)},\frac{\Gamma(s)}{2T^s}\right]$$

and the exact downward recurrence image for $F_m$, from an interval of radius $r_{m+1}$ for $F_{m+1}$, has radius at most
$$\frac{2Tr_{m+1}+r_e}{2m+1}.$$
Outward-rounded intervals add at most the mean of the two endpoint-rounding errors to these radii. Iterating the displayed bounds gives valid finite error-amplification estimates for any requested order range. Upward recurrence is undefined at $T=0$; direct values $F_m(0)=1/(2m+1)$ are exact.

## Statement

Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite TPFA-admissible cell-face mesh, let every cell be connected through interior faces to a cell with a boundary face, and let $T_F>0$ be the transmissibilities of [[def-tpfa-harmonic-face-scheme]]. For cell vectors $u,v$, define
$$ (A_hu)_K=\frac1{|K|}\left(\sum_{F=K|L}T_F(u_K-u_L)+\sum_{F\subset\partial K\cap\partial\Omega}T_{K,F}u_K\right). $$
Then interior fluxes are locally conservative, and for all cell vectors $u,v$,
$$ \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|v_K(A_hu)_K= \sum_{F=K|L\in\mathcal F_{\rm int}}T_F(v_K-v_L)(u_K-u_L) +\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}T_{K,F}v_Ku_K. $$
The stiffness matrix associated with the displayed bilinear identity is symmetric positive definite. Equivalently, $A_h$ is self-adjoint and positive definite in the volume-weighted inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_h=\sum_K|K|u_Kv_K$; its ordinary coordinate matrix need not be symmetric when cell volumes differ. Hence every finite source and boundary-data vector gives a unique solution. If all cell sources and all prescribed boundary face values are nonnegative, then every solution cell value is nonnegative. The maximum-principle claim uses the boundary anchor; no diagonal sign statement alone is used as a substitute for that condition.

## Definition

Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, viscosity $\nu>0$, and time step $k>0$.
Given $u^n\in V_h$ with $D_hu^n=0$, a mean-zero
pressure $p^n\in Q_h$, and a force $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each
have zero discrete mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d),$$
define the next step by the following two solves and update:

1. Find $\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ satisfying
$$ \frac{\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n}{k}+\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}. $$

2. Find the unique $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ satisfying
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$

3. Set
$$ u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-kG_h\phi^{n+1},\qquad p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}. $$

The pressure is kept in $Q_h$ after every solve; the constant pressure mode
is set to zero. The procedure is only asserted for the periodic staggered
grid and the admissible data stated here. The separate well-definedness
theorem [[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies
both solves and the preserved constraints.

## Definition

Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, viscosity $\nu>0$, and time step $k>0$.
Given $u^n\in V_h$ with $D_hu^n=0$, a mean-zero
pressure $p^n\in Q_h$, and a force $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each
have zero discrete mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d),$$
define the next step by the following two solves and update:

1. Find $\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ satisfying
$$ \frac{\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n}{k}+\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}. $$

2. Find the unique $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ satisfying
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$

3. Set
$$ u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-kG_h\phi^{n+1},\qquad p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}. $$

The pressure is kept in $Q_h$ after every solve; the constant pressure mode
is set to zero. The procedure is only asserted for the periodic staggered
grid and the admissible data stated here. The separate well-definedness
theorem [[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies
both solves and the preserved constraints.

## Statement

For real $z>0$, let $h_\ell^{(1)}$ be defined in [[def-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-functions]] and set $h_\ell^{(2)}(z)=\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(z)}$. Then both solve the degree-$\ell$ spherical radial Helmholtz equation, are linearly independent, and
$$\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(z)}(h_\ell^{(1)})'(z)\bigr)=z^{-2}.$$
In particular, neither vanishes for $z>0$, and for $k>0$, $r>0$,
$$r^2\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}\,\partial_r h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)\bigr)=1/k.$$

## Statement

Let $S:=S_1+S_2$, let $\lambda_*$ solve $S\lambda_*=f_1+f_2$, and let $\widetilde\lambda\in\Lambda$ have residual $\rho:=S\widetilde\lambda-(f_1+f_2)$. All trace-vector and operator norms below are induced by the given real inner product on $\Lambda$. Then

$$\|\widetilde\lambda-\lambda_*\|\le\|S^{-1}\|\,\|\rho\|.$$

If each subdomain state is reconstructed by solving its interior equations at the supplied trace, define the product backward-Euler energy norm by $\|(z_1,z_2)\|_{B_1\oplus B_2}^2:=\langle B_1z_1,z_1\rangle+\langle B_2z_2,z_2\rangle$ for $z_i\in X_i$. Then

$$\|\widetilde u-u_*\|_{B_1\oplus B_2}\le\sqrt{\|S^{-1}\|}\,\|\rho\|.$$

## Definition

Let $I_1,I_2$ and the common trace space $\Lambda$ be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, with $\dim\Lambda\ge1$, and set $X_i:=I_i\oplus\Lambda$. The trace map is $\gamma_i(x_i,\lambda_i)=\lambda_i$. Let $M_i$ and $A_i$ be self-adjoint positive-definite operators on $X_i$, let $\Delta t>0$, and define the local backward-Euler block $B_i:=\Delta t^{-1}M_i+A_i$. In coordinates $I_i\oplus\Lambda$, write

$$B_i=\begin{pmatrix}B_{i,00}&B_{i,0\Gamma}\\B_{i,\Gamma0}&B_{i,\Gamma\Gamma}\end{pmatrix},\qquad g_i=(g_{i,0},g_{i,\Gamma}).$$

For a prescribed local trace $\lambda_i$, solve the interior equation $B_{i,00}x_i+B_{i,0\Gamma}\lambda_i=g_{i,0}$ and define the outward algebraic interface flux $q_i:=B_{i,\Gamma0}x_i+B_{i,\Gamma\Gamma}\lambda_i-g_{i,\Gamma}$. Eliminating $x_i$ gives $q_i=S_i\lambda_i-f_i$, where $S_i:=B_{i,\Gamma\Gamma}-B_{i,\Gamma0}B_{i,00}^{-1}B_{i,0\Gamma}$ and $f_i:=g_{i,\Gamma}-B_{i,\Gamma0}B_{i,00}^{-1}g_{i,0}$. The sign convention is outward flux on each subdomain.

The monolithic interface equations are trace continuity $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=\lambda$ and flux balance $q_1+q_2=0$, equivalently $(S_1+S_2)\lambda=f_1+f_2$. These finite-dimensional matrices represent a linear diffusion-transmission step; no nonlinear fluid-structure well-posedness is asserted.

## Statement

Assume Full Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation in two dimensions, let each cell $K$ have an arbitrary finite total degree $p_K\ge1$, and let $u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u|_K\in H^2(K)$ for every cell. For every edge $E$, let $\tau_E$ be either unit tangent direction and write $\partial_{\tau_E}v=\nabla v\cdot\tau_E$. For an interior edge $E=K\cap K'$, set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; for a boundary edge of $K$, set $p_E=p_K$. Put $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. There is a linear interpolant $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$ in the trace-matching space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. It preserves any zero boundary edge data: if $u$ vanishes on a boundary edge, so does $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$. For every $q\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K;\mathbb R)$,

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le |u-q|_{H^1(K)}+C_\gamma\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right),
$$

and

$$
h_K^{-1}\|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)} \le C_\gamma\left(h_K^{-1}\|u-q\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-q|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right)\right).
$$

The constant is independent of the degrees and their ratios. In particular, if integer $r\ge5$, $m_K\ge2r-4$, $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$, and $u|_K\in H^r(K)$, then

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}\left(\frac{(n_K-r+3)!}{(n_K+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

For $m_K\ge4(r-2)$ the factorial factor is at most $(4/m_K)^{r-4}$. The effective degree $m_K$ records the lowest degree among the shared edge traces; no rate independent of neighboring trace degrees is asserted.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. On a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh, let $V=H^1(\Omega)$ with its standard norm, let $a(v,w)=\int_\Omega(\nabla v\cdot\nabla w+vw)$, and let $F$ be a bounded linear functional on $V$. Let $u\in V$ solve $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for all $w\in V$, and let $u_p$ be its conforming Galerkin solution in the common-degree trace-matching tensor space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. If the analytic hypotheses of [[thm-hp-analytic-p-convergence-on-fixed-tensor-mesh]] hold with constants $M,R$ and $R^{-1}<q<1$, then
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathcal T,d,R,q}M q^p.
$$
This is the fixed-mesh analytic branch; it does not assert an h-dependent estimate or an ordinary Sobolev p-rate on simplices.

## Statement

For real $x>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, put

$$(1/2)_0=1,\qquad (1/2)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(j+1/2).$$

$$S_N(x)=\frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} (-1)^k\frac{(1/2)_k}{x^{2k}}.$$

Then

$$\operatorname{erfcx}(x)-S_N(x)=(-1)^N R_N(x),\qquad 0\le R_N(x)\le \frac1{x\sqrt\pi}\frac{(2N)!}{4^N N!x^{2N}}.$$

This is a finite signed remainder bound, not a convergence assertion for the
asymptotic series.

## Statement

For a side state $K=(\rho_K,u_K,p_K)$ and any trial pressure $p>0$, the
rarefaction/shock branches defined in
[[def-euler-star-pressure-response]] give the scalar velocity response
$f_K(p)$ along the corresponding acoustic wave. For a left 1-wave the star velocity is
$u_*=u_L-f_L(p)$; for a right 3-wave it is $u_*=u_R+f_R(p)$. The star density
on a rarefaction branch is
$$\rho_*(p)=\rho_K(p/p_K)^{1/\gamma},$$
and on a compressive shock branch, with $q=p/p_K>1$ and
$\beta=(\gamma-1)/(\gamma+1)$, it is
$$\rho_*(p)=\rho_K\frac{q+\beta}{\beta q+1}.$$
The shock branches satisfy the strict acoustic Lax inequalities. When the two
pressure responses match at a positive $p$, their star states are joined by a
linearly-degenerate contact at speed $u_*$.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, put $p'=p/(p-1)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ for $T>0$. Let $a(x,\xi)$ satisfy the Carathéodory, $p$-growth, coercivity, and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]].

For each $m$, let $\mathcal P_m$ be a finite measurable partition of $\Omega$ into cells of positive measure and let a finite time partition carry cell values. Let $\bar U_m$ be the function constant on each resulting space-time cell. Suppose there are conforming reconstructions $w_m\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and a function $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$ \bar U_m\to u\text{ strongly in }L^p(0,T;H),\qquad \|\bar U_m-w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;H)}\to0, $$
and $\sup_m\|w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;V)}<\infty$. Write $\xi_m=\nabla w_m$ and $q_m=a(x,\xi_m)$. Assume, along the same subsequence, $q_m\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$ and
$$ \limsup_{m\to\infty}\int_Qq_m\cdot\xi_m\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u. $$
Finally, assume $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $u_0\in H$, and the finite-volume weak identities have residuals $r_m(\varphi)\to0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$:
$$ -\int_Q\bar U_m\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_m\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=r_m(\varphi). $$
Then $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere, and $u$ is a weak evolution solution of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$ with initial trace $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]:
$$ -\int_Q u\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_Qf\varphi+\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx $$
for every such test function. This is a conditional finite-volume limit-identification result; the reconstruction, residual, compactness, and energy hypotheses are not conclusions of the statement.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, put $p'=p/(p-1)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with gradient norm, $H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$ for $T>0$. Let $a(x,\xi)$ satisfy the Carathéodory, $p$-growth, coercivity, and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]].

For each $m$, let $\mathcal P_m$ be a finite measurable partition of $\Omega$ into cells of positive measure and let a finite time partition carry cell values. Let $\bar U_m$ be the function constant on each resulting space-time cell. Suppose there are conforming reconstructions $w_m\in L^p(0,T;V)$ and a function $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$ \bar U_m\to u\text{ strongly in }L^p(0,T;H),\qquad \|\bar U_m-w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;H)}\to0, $$
and $\sup_m\|w_m\|_{L^p(0,T;V)}<\infty$. Write $\xi_m=\nabla w_m$ and $q_m=a(x,\xi_m)$. Assume, along the same subsequence, $q_m\rightharpoonup q$ in $L^{p'}(Q;\mathbb R^d)$ and
$$ \limsup_{m\to\infty}\int_Qq_m\cdot\xi_m\le\int_Qq\cdot\nabla u. $$
Finally, assume $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $u_0\in H$, and the finite-volume weak identities have residuals $r_m(\varphi)\to0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty([0,T)\times\Omega)$:
$$ -\int_Q\bar U_m\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qq_m\cdot\nabla\varphi-\int_Qf\varphi-\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx=r_m(\varphi). $$
Then $q=a(x,\nabla u)$ almost everywhere, and $u$ is a weak evolution solution of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$ with initial trace $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]:
$$ -\int_Q u\,\partial_t\varphi+\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_Qf\varphi+\int_\Omega u_0(x)\varphi(x,0)\,dx $$
for every such test function. This is a conditional finite-volume limit-identification result; the reconstruction, residual, compactness, and energy hypotheses are not conclusions of the statement.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let TPFA-admissible meshes also form a regular simplicial companion family, with homogeneous Dirichlet data and fixed $0<\lambda_*\le\lambda_K\le\lambda^*$. If cell vectors $v_h$ satisfy $\sup_h\|v_h\|_{E_h}<\infty$, there are a subsequence and $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ such that $\Pi_hv_h\to v$ strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$, and the gradients of the conforming companions converge weakly to $\nabla v$ in $L^2$.

There is also an explicit physical weak-gradient reconstruction. Let $P_{K,F}$ be the pyramid with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$, ignoring its measure-zero boundary. For $F=K|L$ put $\mathcal D_F=P_{K,F}\cup P_{L,F}$, fix the normal $n=n_{K,F}$, and define
$$\mathcal G_hv=d\frac{v_L-v_K}{d_F}n\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D_F.$$
On a boundary pyramid put $\mathcal G_hv=-dv_Kn_{K,F}/d_{K,F}$. These regions partition $\Omega$ up to null sets. Along the same subsequence $\mathcal G_hv_h\rightharpoonup\nabla v$ in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\|\mathcal G_hv_h\|_2^2=d\left(\sum_{F=K|L}\frac{|F|}{d_F}|v_L-v_K|^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}|v_K|^2\right)\le\frac d{\lambda_*}\|v_h\|_{E_h}^2.$$
The dimension factor $d$ is essential. This physical gradient differs from the face-copy bookkeeping gradient in the TPFA Definition; no identification of that separate copy space with $\Omega$ is asserted.

Let K be a nonempty compact convex subset of the positive-density domain of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]]. Use ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_{z∈K}max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇W_ε||∞, K₂=||D²W_ε||∞, and a(ρ,e)=P(ρ,e)/ρ². Define A₀=max_{z∈K,,i}|a(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_ρ=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ρa(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_e=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ea(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, and A_Lip=2MK₁A_ρ+A_e. By [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], these suprema are finite and the displayed maxima are attained, since K is nonempty compact and the functions involved are continuous. Then the full state vector field F is Lipschitz on K with constant

$$L=\max\{1,\ M(2K_1A_{\mathrm{Lip}}+4A_0K_2),\ 2MVA_{\mathrm{Lip}}K_1+2MA_0K_1+4MA_0VK_2\}.$$

Let K be a nonempty compact convex subset of the positive-density domain of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]]. Use ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_{z∈K}max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇W_ε||∞, K₂=||D²W_ε||∞, and a(ρ,e)=P(ρ,e)/ρ². Define A₀=max_{z∈K,,i}|a(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_ρ=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ρa(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_e=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ea(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, and A_Lip=2MK₁A_ρ+A_e. By [[thm-extreme-value-metric]], these suprema are finite and the displayed maxima are attained, since K is nonempty compact and the functions involved are continuous. Then the full state vector field F is Lipschitz on K with constant

$$L=\max\{1,\ M(2K_1A_{\mathrm{Lip}}+4A_0K_2),\ 2MVA_{\mathrm{Lip}}K_1+2MA_0K_1+4MA_0VK_2\}.$$

## Statement

Take $A=[1]$, $B=[1]$, $M_Q=[1]$, and $\gamma=1$ in the symmetric
saddle-point and block-preconditioning convention of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Interpret
$V=Q=\mathbb R$ with Euclidean norms, $a(v,w)=vw$, and $b(v,q)=qv$; thus the
pressure-Schur hypotheses hold with $\alpha=\Lambda=C_b=\beta=1$. Then
$$ K=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_1=I. $$
The symmetrically preconditioned eigenvalues are
$$ \frac{1-\sqrt5}{2},\qquad\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}. $$
For right-hand side $(1,0)^T$, the unique saddle solution is $(u,p)=(0,1)$.
This exact example illustrates the spectrum only; it implies no solver-speed
or iteration-count claim.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be the bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain and
$\mathcal T_h$ a finite matching shape-regular simplicial mesh of
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]]. For every $v_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$ there is
a continuous piecewise affine function $E_hv_h$ with zero boundary trace
such that
$$\|\nabla E_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|v_h-E_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C h\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},$$
where $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K$. In particular,
$E_hv_h\in H^1_0(\Omega)$.

## Example

## Definition

For $k>0$, $R>0$, and $g\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C)$, let $g_\ell$ be its $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$-orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_\ell$ and set
$$\tau_\ell(k,R)=k\frac{(h_\ell^{(1)})'(kR)}{h_\ell^{(1)}(kR)},\qquad T_{k,R}g=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\tau_\ell(k,R)g_\ell.$$
The associated outgoing extension for $r\ge R$ is
$$v(r,\omega)=\sum_{\ell=0}^\infty\frac{h_\ell^{(1)}(kr)}{h_\ell^{(1)}(kR)}g_\ell(\omega).$$
The denominator is nonzero by [[lem-pe18-spherical-hankel-radial-identities]]. The convergence, smoothness, PDE, and radiation properties are asserted in [[thm-pe18-exact-spherical-dtn-map-on-smooth-data]].

## Definition

Use the model of [[def-na-periodic-diagonal-controlled-diffusion-hjb-problem]] and a periodic grid with $N_j\ge3$, $h_j=1/N_j$, and step $\tau>0$. For a nodal array $V$, define
$$D_{jj}^hV_i=\frac{V_{i+e_j}-2V_i+V_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.$$
For a control $a$, define
$$D_{j,a}^{up}V_i=\begin{cases}(V_i-V_{i-e_j})/h_j,&b_j^a(x_i,t_n)\ge0,\\(V_{i+e_j}-V_i)/h_j,&b_j^a(x_i,t_n)<0.\end{cases}$$
The recurrence is
$$U_i^{n+1}=U_i^n+\tau\max_{a\in A}\left\{\sum_{j=1}^d\left[\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n)D_{jj}^hU_i+b_j^a(x_i,t_n)D_{j,a}^{up}U_i\right]+f^a(x_i,t_n)\right\}.$$
Admit a step only when, at every node, control, and coordinate,
$$|b_j^a(x_i,t_n)|h_j\le\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n),$$
and
$$\tau\max_{i,a}\sum_{j=1}^d\left(\frac{2\alpha_j^a(x_i,t_n)}{h_j^2}+\frac{|b_j^a(x_i,t_n)|}{h_j}\right)\le1.$$
Initialize by $U_i^0=u_0(x_i)$ and perform the finite number of updates specified by the time horizon. No claim about an arbitrary anisotropic central stencil is included.

## Example

On the unit cubic torus take charges $q_1=1$ at $x_1=(0,0,0)$ and $q_2=-1$ at
$x_2=(1/2,0,0)$. For $r=|x-x_1|\downarrow0$, the exact Ewald potential and its
gradient satisfy
$$U_\alpha(x)=\frac1r+O(1),\qquad \nabla_xU_\alpha(x)=-\frac{x-x_1}{r^3}+O(1).$$
The potential and field therefore have their local Coulomb singularities, so
a pointwise potential or field-error claim must exclude a source collision.

## Statement

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, star-shaped with respect to a ball, and let $\omega$ and $\mathcal B_U$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. Under Countable Choice there is a bounded linear extension $\mathcal B_U:L^2_0(U)\to H^1_0(U;\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$\operatorname{div}\mathcal B_U f=f,\qquad \|\nabla\mathcal B_U f\|_2\le C_U\|f\|_2.$$
After translating the ball center to $0$, choose $R_U\ge\sup_{y\in U}|y|$ and define
$$A_j(\phi)=2^{(d-1)/2}\bigl(\rho^{-1}\|\phi\|_1+\rho\|\partial_j^2\phi\|_1\bigr)+2^d|U|\|\partial_j\phi\|_\infty.$$
One valid constant is $C_U=\left(\sum_{k,j=1}^d[A_j(x_k\omega)+R_UA_j(\omega)]^2\right)^{1/2}$.

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, star-shaped with respect to a ball, and let $\omega$ and $\mathcal B_U$ be as in [[def-na-star-shaped-bogovskii-integral]]. Under Countable Choice there is a bounded linear extension $\mathcal B_U:L^2_0(U)\to H^1_0(U;\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$\operatorname{div}\mathcal B_U f=f,\qquad \|\nabla\mathcal B_U f\|_2\le C_U\|f\|_2.$$
After translating the ball center to $0$, choose $R_U\ge\sup_{y\in U}|y|$ and define
$$A_j(\phi)=2^{(d-1)/2}\bigl(\rho^{-1}\|\phi\|_1+\rho\|\partial_j^2\phi\|_1\bigr)+2^d|U|\|\partial_j\phi\|_\infty.$$
One valid constant is $C_U=\left(\sum_{k,j=1}^d[A_j(x_k\omega)+R_UA_j(\omega)]^2\right)^{1/2}$.

## Statement

Let $(\eta,q)$ be a convex entropy pair on an open set $\mathcal A$, with
entropy variable $v$ and potential $\psi$ as in
[[def-pe03-system-entropy-pair-and-potential]]. On a periodic mesh of $N\ge2$
cells of width $\Delta x>0$, let differentiable states $U_i(t)\in\mathcal A$
satisfy
$$\dot U_i=-\frac{F^{es}_{i+1/2}-F^{es}_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x},$$
where every face flux is the entropy-stable dissipative flux of
[[def-pe03-entropy-stable-dissipative-flux]]. Define
$$\widehat q_{i+1/2}:=\left(\frac{v_i+v_{i+1}}2\right)^T F^{es}_{i+1/2}-\frac{\psi_i+\psi_{i+1}}2.$$
Then each cell satisfies
$$\frac{d}{dt}\eta(U_i)+\frac{\widehat q_{i+1/2}-\widehat q_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x}\le0.$$
Summing over the periodic mesh gives nonincrease of total discrete entropy.
This is a semidiscrete result; it asserts no entropy inequality for a chosen
fully discrete time integrator.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded
Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular refining family of matching affine
tetrahedral meshes $\mathcal T_h$, with maximum cell diameter $h\to0$. For
every $w\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, the canonical lowest-order
Nedelec edge interpolant $I_hw$, defined by its six oriented edge
circulations on each tetrahedron, is well-defined. For all sufficiently
small $h$ it belongs to $H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$, and
$$\|I_hw-w\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.$$
The edge moments are applied only to smooth fields here; this statement does
not extend them to arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ inputs.

## Statement

Under exactly the hypotheses of [[lem-hybrid-mimetic-backward-euler-energy-and-compactness]], the computed cell states converge, along a subsequence, to a weak evolution solution $u$ of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$, $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. In addition to the strong state convergences in that lemma, the actual constitutive fields
$$q_h(t,x)=a(x,G_KU_h^n)\quad(t\in(t_{n-1},t_n],\ x\in K)$$
converge weakly in $L^{p'}(Q)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\longrightarrow\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \sum_n\tau_n S_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\longrightarrow0.$$
The final cell states converge strongly to $u(T)$ in $H$.

This includes convergence of a physical reconstruction of the actual numerical face fluxes. Let $r_{K,F}=x_F-x_K$, $s_{K,F}^n=\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n))$, $b_K^n=b_K(G_KU_h^n)$, and $c_K^n=|K|^{-1}\sum_Fs_{K,F}^nr_{K,F}$. On the physical pyramid $P_{K,F}$ with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$ set
$$q_h^{\rm num}=b_K^n-c_K^n+\frac{s_{K,F}^n}{|F|}n_{K,F}.$$
Then $-|F|q_h^{\rm num}|_{P_{K,F}}\cdot n_{K,F}=Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(U_h^n)$ exactly, $q_h^{\rm num}-b_h\to0$ strongly in $L^{p'}(Q)$, with $b_h|_K=b_K^n$, and $q_h^{\rm num}\rightharpoonup a(x,\nabla u)$ in $L^{p'}(Q)$. No strong convergence of $G_h\overline U_h$ is inferred from mere monotonicity.

Finally the hypotheses of [[lem-mimetic-fv-parabolic-limit-identification]] can be supplied on this same subsequence by conforming limit recovery: take $w_h=u$ and $\widetilde q_h=a(x,\nabla w_h)=a(x,\nabla u)$. These are post-limit conforming functions, distinct from the computed companions $E_h\overline U_h$, constitutive fields $q_h$, and numerical fluxes $q_h^{\rm num}$. The computed convergence assertion above is established independently of this recovery observation.

## Statement

For the data of [[def-overlapping-schwarz-subspace-correction-data]], assume
$\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}V_i=V$. Let
$R=[R_i]_{i\in\mathcal I}$ and
$\mathcal D=\operatorname{diag}(A_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$, so
$B=R\mathcal D^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}$. Then $B$ is SPD and, for every $x\in V$,
$$ x^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}x = \min_{\substack{z=(z_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}\\Rz=x}} \sum_{i\in\mathcal I}z_i^{\mathsf T}A_i z_i. $$

## Definition

Work in exact real arithmetic. Let $n\ge1$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$, and let

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the weak elliptic existence suppliers used to instantiate either model branch.

Let $(\mathcal T_k,U_k)$ be generated by exact P1 Galerkin solves and the three-generation algorithm with $\theta_E,\theta_O\in(0,1]$, and assume every per-call bisection budget is sufficient for a complete refinement. For the estimator and oscillation of [[def-afem-p1-residual-estimator-and-data-oscillation]], write $e_k=\|\nabla(u-U_k)\|_2$, $\eta_k=\eta(U_k,\mathcal T_k)$ and $\operatorname{osc}_k=\operatorname{osc}(U_k,\mathcal T_k)$. On the symmetric branch $b=0$, no initial-mesh smallness is needed. On the constant-convection branch assume the uniform dual-pickup bound of [[lem-afem-convection-quasi-orthogonality-under-fine-mesh]] and set $\mu=C_Dh_0^s|b|$. Define
$$\kappa=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{\theta_E}{C_{\rm eff}C_{\rm rel}}\right\},\qquad \nu=\begin{cases}0,&b=0,\\ \mu/(1-\mu),&b\ne0.\end{cases}$$
In the convection branch assume $\mu<1$, so that $\nu$ is defined and the quasi-orthogonality estimate applies, and assume $\nu<\kappa$. Then there are $\beta>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$, depending only on the displayed constants and marking parameters, such that
$$e_{k+1}^2+\beta\operatorname{osc}_{k+1}^2 \le\alpha\big(e_k^2+\beta\operatorname{osc}_{k}^2\big).$$

Moreover, after possibly reducing a positive weight $\sigma$, there are $\beta'>0$ and $0<\alpha'<1$ such that
$$e_{k+1}^2+\beta'\operatorname{osc}_{k+1}^2+\sigma\eta_{k+1}^2 \le\alpha'\big(e_k^2+\beta'\operatorname{osc}_{k}^2+\sigma\eta_k^2\big).$$
This second assertion records the residual-estimator reduction as part of the usual AFEM quasi-error. Constants and smallness hypotheses belong to the chosen marking and the stated dual-pickup bound.

## Definition

For $\lambda\in H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $\phi\in H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$ define the Laplace Calderon boundary operators by
$$V\lambda=\gamma S\lambda,\qquad K\phi=\tfrac12(\gamma^-D\phi+\gamma^+D\phi),$$
$$K'\lambda=\tfrac12(\partial_n^-S\lambda+\partial_n^+S\lambda),\qquad W\phi=-\partial_n^-D\phi=-\partial_n^+D\phi.$$
Here $\gamma S\lambda$ is the common trace, conormal traces use the orientation of [[def-bem-lipschitz-polyhedral-boundary-and-trace-spaces]], and the last equality is meaningful because the weak double layer has a common conormal derivative. This page uses the real duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)$ and $H^{1/2}(\Gamma)$. The well-definedness and bounded mapping properties of $V,K,K',W$ are proved in [[thm-bem-calderon-mapping-and-jump-identities]].

## Definition

This procedure defines a real-arithmetic finite-dimensional FE-HMM discretization. It makes no bit-complexity claim, no coefficient-oracle claim, and no claim about numerically computing its exact integral entries; those entries are the mathematical values of the displayed integrals. Fix $Q=(0,1)^2$ and coefficient $a$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]]. Use the diagonal of the square from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$ as a two-triangle initial matching macro mesh. Label that shared diagonal $0$ in both triangles and each exterior edge $1$. It is a compatible labeled mesh in the sense of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. The macro input is any finite admissible descendant triangulation $\mathcal T$ of this mesh. Its cells are closed affine triangles as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].

Choose $\epsilon>0$, a micro side length $\delta>0$, $f\in L^2(Q)$, and a finite matching triangulation $\mathcal M$ of the unit square whose opposite boundary edges and vertices match under translation by $e_1,e_2$. The periodic micro space is
$$W_{\mathcal M}:=\{z\in V_\#:z\text{ is continuous and affine on every triangle of }\mathcal M\}.$$
It is a finite-dimensional subspace of $V_\#$; the periodic closure condition identifies opposite traces. Let $V_H$ be the conforming zero-boundary continuous piecewise-affine macro space on $\mathcal T$, using [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Its inclusion in $H^1_0(Q)$ is supplied by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]].

Identify vertices of $\mathcal M$ that match under the opposite-edge translations, and order the resulting periodic vertex classes by the lexicographically least representative of each class. Let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N$ be the continuous periodic P1 nodal functions for these classes, with $\phi_i=1$ at class $i$ and $0$ at the other classes. Set $m_i=\int_Y\phi_i\,dy$. If $N=1$, use the empty basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$; otherwise use
$$\psi_i:=\phi_i-\frac{m_i}{m_1}\phi_1\qquad(2\le i\le N)$$
as the ordered basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$. The nodal basis spans the full periodic P1 space, and these functions form a basis of its mean-zero subspace.

Use the following exact solver on the systems assembled below. Given a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb R^n$, `ExactSolve(A,b)` returns the empty vector if $n=0$. Otherwise form the augmented matrix $[A\mid b]$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least row index $p\ge k$ whose current entry in column $k$ is nonzero; if there is no such row, return `singular-system`. Swap rows $p$ and $k$. For each $i=k+1,\ldots,n$, set $r=A_{ik}/A_{kk}$, replace augmented row $i$ by row $i-r\,\mathrm{row}_k$, and set its column-$k$ entry to zero. After this loop, compute $x_n,x_{n-1},\ldots,x_1$ by backward substitution in the resulting upper-triangular system and return $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. All arithmetic and zero tests are exact over $\mathbb R$; the systems assembled below are positive definite.

Order macro triangles by lexicographic order of their barycenters. For each such $K$, use its barycenter $x_K$ as the single quadrature point with positive weight $|K|$, and set
$$b_K(y):=a\!\left(\frac{x_K}{\epsilon}+\frac{\delta}{\epsilon}y\right)\quad(y\in Y).$$
The affine change-of-variables theorem [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] makes this a measurable coefficient class independent of the representative of $a$, with $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere. For each coordinate vector $e_j$, in order $j=1,2$, assemble
$$G^K_{i\ell}:=\int_Yb_K\nabla\psi_\ell\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy,\qquad r^K_{i,j}:=-\int_Yb_K e_j\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy$$
over the micro-basis indices $2\le i,\ell\le N$. If that basis is empty, set $w^h_{K,j}=0$; otherwise call `ExactSolve(G^K,r^K_{\cdot,j})`, index its returned coordinates by $2,\ldots,N$, and set $w^h_{K,j}=\sum_{\ell=2}^N x_\ell\psi_\ell$. Then set
$$A^h_Ke_j:=\int_Yb_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j}(y))\,dy.$$
The `singular-system` branch is included to make the solver instruction total; [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves it is not reached for these micro systems.

Order the interior vertices of $\mathcal T$ lexicographically and let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_M$ be the corresponding nodal basis of $V_H$. If $M=0$, set $U_H=0$. Otherwise assemble
$$H_{rs}:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla\varphi_s|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla\varphi_r|_K,\qquad F_r:=\int_Qf\varphi_r\,dx,$$
call `ExactSolve(H,F)`, and set $U_H:=\sum_{s=1}^M x_s\varphi_s$. This basis system is exactly the variational system
$$B_H(U,V)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla U|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla V|_K=\int_QfV\qquad(V\in V_H).$$
The macro matrix is positive definite and its `singular-system` branch is unreachable by [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Output $U_H$. The centroid quadrature is positive and exact for constants, which is the only quadrature property used in the error theorem.

Order macro triangles by lexicographic order of their barycenters. For each such $K$, use its barycenter $x_K$ as the single quadrature point with positive weight $|K|$, and set
$$b_K(y):=a\!\left(\frac{x_K}{\epsilon}+\frac{\delta}{\epsilon}y\right)\quad(y\in Y).$$
The affine change-of-variables theorem [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] makes this a measurable coefficient class independent of the representative of $a$, with $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere. For each coordinate vector $e_j$, in order $j=1,2$, assemble
$$G^K_{i\ell}:=\int_Yb_K\nabla\psi_\ell\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy,\qquad r^K_{i,j}:=-\int_Yb_K e_j\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy$$
over the micro-basis indices $2\le i,\ell\le N$. If that basis is empty, set $w^h_{K,j}=0$; otherwise call `ExactSolve(G^K,r^K_{\cdot,j})`, index its returned coordinates by $2,\ldots,N$, and set $w^h_{K,j}=\sum_{\ell=2}^N x_\ell\psi_\ell$. Then set
$$A^h_Ke_j:=\int_Yb_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j}(y))\,dy.$$
The `singular-system` branch is included to make the solver instruction total; [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves it is not reached for these micro systems.

Order the interior vertices of $\mathcal T$ lexicographically and let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_M$ be the corresponding nodal basis of $V_H$. If $M=0$, set $U_H=0$. Otherwise assemble
$$H_{rs}:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla\varphi_s|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla\varphi_r|_K,\qquad F_r:=\int_Qf\varphi_r\,dx,$$
call `ExactSolve(H,F)`, and set $U_H:=\sum_{s=1}^M x_s\varphi_s$. This basis system is exactly the variational system
$$B_H(U,V)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla U|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla V|_K=\int_QfV\qquad(V\in V_H).$$
The macro matrix is positive definite and its `singular-system` branch is unreachable by [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Output $U_H$. The centroid quadrature is positive and exact for constants, which is the only quadrature property used in the error theorem.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty
bounded open set, $d\ge1$, and let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$. The flux
$a(x,\xi)=|\xi|^{p-2}\xi$, with $a(x,0)=0$, satisfies the coercivity,
monotonicity and $p$-growth hypotheses in
[[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]], and its induced operator is additionally norm-continuous. Its zero-boundary space embeds
compactly into $L^2(\Omega)$. In particular, on the nonempty interval
$\Omega=(0,1)$ for $d=1$, or the nonempty unit cube $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ for
$d\ge2$, the explicit fixed-degree interval or Kuhn/Freudenthal meshes and
any independent time partitions with vanishing maximum step satisfy the
projector hypotheses. The convergence theorem
[[thm-pe12-monotone-fem-limit]] therefore applies on those concrete meshes
for every load and initial datum in its stated classes; no projector
condition remains outstanding in this example.

## Example

Let $x$ be periodic, $0<y<L$, and fix $p_0>0$, $T_w>0$, $a\ne0$, $\mu>0$, and $\kappa>0$. Define

$$u(x,y)=(ay,0),\qquad T(y)=T_w+\frac{\mu a^2}{2\kappa}y(L-y),\qquad \rho(y)=\frac{p_0}{RT(y)},$$

and $m=\rho u$, $E=p_0/(\gamma-1)+\rho a^2y^2/2$. This is a smooth positive steady solution with constant pressure $p_0$, no-slip wall velocities $u(x,0)=(0,0)$ and $u(x,L)=(aL,0)$, and wall temperature $T_w$ at both walls. Per unit periodic length, the outward physical-entropy flux through the two thermal walls equals

$$\left[-\kappa\frac{T'}{T}\right]_{0}^{L} =\int_0^L\left(\frac{\mu a^2}{T}+\frac{\kappa(T')^2}{T^2}\right)dy>0.$$

This is a continuous wall-balance example; it specifies no discrete wall flux.

## Statement

Every differentiable solution of [[def-orthogonal-fv-compressible-viscous-scheme]] with $U_i(t)\in\mathcal G$ satisfies

$$\frac{d}{dt}\sum_{i=1}^N h\eta(U_i) =-\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\frac{(v_{i+1}-v_i)^TK_{i+1/2}(v_{i+1}-v_i)}{h}\le0, \qquad \frac{d}{dt}\sum_{i=1}^N hU_i=0.$$

If every cell/node state of $U^n$ lies in $R$, then every cell/node state of $U^{n+1}$ lies in $R$ for every finite $\tau\ge0$. If $c^TF=0$ throughout $R$, then $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^{n+1})=\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^n)$; if $c^TF\le0$ throughout $R$, then $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^{n+1})\le\mathcal M_{c,h}(U^n)$. Here $\mathcal M_{c,h}(U)=\sum_i m_i c^TU_i$ uses the cell/node weights of the chosen discretization.

## Definition

Let $F:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be locally Lipschitz, and let $R=\prod_{i=1}^m[a_i,b_i]\subset U$ with finite $a_i<b_i$. The rectangle is **reaction-inward** if, for every $i$, $F_i(z)\ge0$ on the lower face $z_i=a_i$ and $F_i(z)\le0$ on the upper face $z_i=b_i$, with all other coordinates in their intervals. It is **reaction-invariant** if the solution map $\Phi_F^t$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ on $R$ and $\Phi_F^t(R)\subseteq R$ for every $t\ge0$.

For a rectangle with $a_i=0$ for all $i$, the lower-face condition is exactly quasi-positivity from [[def-reaction-vector-field-and-quasipositivity]]. The upper-face condition is independent and must be checked separately. The inward-sign condition is a hypothesis, not by definition an invariance theorem.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the real displacement formulation of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]] on a nonempty bounded, connected Lipschitz domain $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. Let $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ with the gradient norm, let the measurable shear modulus satisfy $0<\mu_0\le\mu(x)\le\mu_1<\infty$ almost everywhere, let $0\le\lambda<\infty$, and let $f\in V'$. For a finite conforming isogeometric subspace $V_h\subset V$ built from the matching NURBS patches of [[def-isogeometric-galerkin-patch-space-and-refinement]], the elasticity variational problem has a unique solution $u$, the Galerkin problem has a unique solution $u_h$, and
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{2\mu_1+d\lambda}{\mu_0}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The estimate is for each finite $\lambda$ and has a factor growing with $\lambda$; it is not a locking-free or $\lambda$-uniform NURBS result.

## Example

Let $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(0,1)$, and
$D=(1,1+\delta)$ with $\delta=2^{-52}$. Their raw lifted determinant with
rows $(x,y,x^2+y^2,1)$ is $-(\delta+\delta^2)$. In a 113-bit filter format
with $u=2^{-113}$ and a normal range covering the displayed operations, every
lifted entry is exactly representable. The filter error radius is less than
$\delta/4$, so it certifies the negative lifted sign; since the base
orientation is positive, the last site is outside the circle through $A,B,C$.
