## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Inputs are a full-rank real cell matrix $A$, a finite
neutral configuration of pairwise-distinct torus positions $x_i$ and real
charges $q_i$, an Ewald parameter $\alpha>0$, cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, integers
$M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, a mesh-self-correction flag, an optional off-source
query point $x$, requested nonnegative tolerances for each requested output,
and integer controller indices $J_R\ge\lfloor R\rfloor$,
$J_K\ge\lfloor K_c\rfloor$, and $J_A\ge1$. The inputs must satisfy
$2\alpha^2J_R(J_R+1)\ge3$ and
$(2\alpha^2)^{-1}J_K(J_K+1)\ge3$ for the shell controllers. The arithmetic
interface is one fixed instance of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]],
with representable set $\mathbb F$ and certified outward enclosures for every
finite arithmetic node, elementary-function evaluation, transform phase, and
final arithmetic radius. There is an optional positive integer enclosure-work
cap $B_{\mathrm{encl}}$, defaulting to $1$ when omitted. Each non-transform
validation, enclosure, or comparison request executes its supplied certificate
lookup/evaluation program for at most $B_{\mathrm{encl}}$ program
instructions, including control-flow steps. Its numerical primitives are exact
rational arithmetic/comparisons, fixed-format rounded operations, and reads of
finite supplied certificate data. Elementary functions
and refinement loops are implemented through these counted instructions, not
as uncapped oracle calls. On exhaustion, unavailable data, a nonfinite bound,
an uncertified required divisor or an unresolved comparison, return
`arithmetic-inconclusive`, except where an explicit cutoff, transform, or
window-denominator branch below names its more specific status. Do not retry
with larger budgets inside a run. A larger cap may be supplied for another
run; no accepted enclosure loses its required soundness. Supplied finite
certificate data and the cap are part of the arithmetic interface, so this
rule does not impose a precision or accuracy restriction on successful outputs. Every particle and optional query point also has a
certified representative interval in $[0,1)^3$ after reduction modulo the
cell. Transform calls use common controls: an exact rational phase tolerance
$\tau$ with $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer exponent limits $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$,
integer precision $p_0\ge2$, finite integer cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, integer
elementary-series cap $J_{\mathrm{phase}}\ge1$, and integer radix-two depth
$d_{\max}\ge0$ required by
[[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]]. Every vector passed to a
transform has real and imaginary coordinates in $\mathbb F$, and the outward
enclosures include phase and arithmetic errors from the entire transform call.
If $\sum_iq_i\ne0$ is certified, return `nonneutral`. Otherwise check
neutrality, distinctness, full rank, valid scalar/integer controls, and the
required input enclosures using the bounded interface above. A certified
violation of these input conditions returns `invalid-input`; unavailable or
unresolved evidence returns `arithmetic-inconclusive`. If a query point is
certified to be a source image, return `collision` for that potential query;
if its off-source status is unresolved, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`.
A controller inequality that is certified false is `invalid-input`; an
unresolved one is `arithmetic-inconclusive`.

1. Compute a certified outward upper bound $B_K$ for $\|A^T\|_2K_c/(2\pi)$ and set $N_K=\lceil B_K\rceil$. Enumerate every integer triple in the finite box $[-N_K,N_K]^3$. For each nonzero $k$, compute a certified interval $[d_k^-,d_k^+]$ for $|2\pi A^{-T}k|$ and an interval $[K_c^-,K_c^+]$ for $K_c$. Include $k$ in $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ if $d_k^+\le K_c^-$, exclude it if $d_k^->K_c^+$, and return `cutoff-inconclusive` if neither comparison is certified. Retain from $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ exactly the signed modes satisfying $|k_r|<M_r/2$ for every coordinate and store them in $\mathcal K$. This set is finite, symmetric and injective modulo the mesh. Every other mode in $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ is kept in the finite omitted-mode ledger $\mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K$; it is never assigned zero error.

2. Initialize the full grid $g$ to zero. Use each particle's supplied certified representative interval $t_i\in[0,1)^3$. For each coordinate $r$, enclose $a=M_rt_{i,r}$ by $[a^-,a^+]$; if $a^+-a^->1$, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Enumerate every integer $L_r$ from $\lceil a^- -P\rceil$ through $\lfloor a^+\rfloor$. This finite list contains every translate with $0\le a-L_r\le P$ and has at most $P+2$ entries. For every triple $(L_1,L_2,L_3)$, evaluate $q_i\prod_rW_P(M_rt_{i,r}-L_r)$, reduce $L_r$ modulo $M_r$ to the grid residue $\ell_r$, add the term to $g_\ell$, and store the particle's finite support tuples for later gathers. This Cartesian list computes the periodic assignment exactly because each integer $L_r$ is uniquely $\ell_r+jM_r$. Accumulate all terms that wrap to the same residue; when $P>M_r$, do not drop duplicate contributions. The support is the causal predecessor support of the window, not an unspecified symmetric nearest-node rule.

3. For each coordinate fiber, call [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] with the supplied common transform controls on its representable center vector. If an input cannot be represented, a call returns any `inconclusive` or `range-failure` status, or a normalization scale fails, return `transform-inconclusive` and retain that substatus. Apply the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},\qquad N_g=M_1M_2M_3,$$
by dividing each returned unnormalised coordinate transform by $\sqrt{M_r}$, with outward enclosures for every scale operation. The required mathematical output convention is the unitary transform. The correctness-and-cost supplier proves the formal exact-constant transform identity; it is not used as a floating-point error bound.

4. For each retained $k$, form the window multiplier
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P$$
and obtain an outward lower bound for $|D(k)|$. If any lower bound is nonpositive, return `denominator-inconclusive` without division. Otherwise set
$$z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}},\qquad c_k=\frac{4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{V|\kappa_k|^2}.$$
Use the conjugated denominator forced by the negative-sign DFT and the causal window. The signed mode representative is used in every window factor; residues are used only as storage indices.

5. For every tensor-transform call in this step, use [[alg-na-computed-fast-transforms-and-convolution]] with the same model and controls as in Step 3, divide each coordinate output by $\sqrt{M_r}$, and propagate a failed or unrepresentable subcall or failed normalization as `transform-inconclusive`. Form mode arrays on the full mesh-frequency grid, placing retained signed modes in their unique residues and setting all other entries to zero. Set $v^U_k=c_kz_k/D(k)$ on $\mathcal K$. Apply the per-coordinate unitary normalization to the negative-sign tensor DFT of $\overline{v^U}$, conjugate the output, and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$; the inverse-transform target array is $u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^U_ke^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. If a query point was supplied, use its supplied representative $t_x$ and the finite-support routine of Step 2 to compute the off-source mesh potential $\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t_x)u_\ell$. For forces set $v^F_k=c_k\overline{z_k}/\overline{D(k)}$ on $\mathcal K$, zero elsewhere, and apply the same per-coordinate normalization to its negative-sign tensor DFT, then multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form $\lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^F_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. Evaluate $\nabla_xw_\ell$ by differentiating the finite support products on the selected mesh box and applying $A^{-T}$; aggregate all tuple derivative contributions by residue, retaining duplicate wraps. Then $F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i)$, gathering only the at most $(P+2)^3$ candidate support contributions per particle. For $P=2$ at a knot, use the one-sided derivative from the adjacent box immediately to the right in each knot coordinate (box index $\lfloor M_rt_r\rfloor$ modulo $M_r$), consistently for the full derivative vector and both correction factors. Determine this right-hand mesh-box index by the bounded certificate interface, allowing a supplied exact knot equality; if its floor/branch cannot be certified, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. This is the selected branch from the assignment definition and is not asserted to be a classical gradient. Computed enclosures retain outward bounds on residual imaginary parts. The mesh energy is $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$.

   If mesh-self correction is enabled, place $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on retained residues and zero elsewhere. Apply the same normalized negative-sign tensor DFT to $h$ and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form the cyclic kernel $\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r}$. For each particle evaluate $S_i=\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$ over all support-residue pairs, retaining duplicate-wrap contributions, and set $C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2(S_i-\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k)$. Replace the mesh energy by $E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M$. Replace the uncorrected force by $F_{M,i}+q_i^2\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$, using the same selected derivative branch. The equality of this finite cyclic-kernel computation with the correction and its branch derivative is proved in [[thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-error-bound]]. Outward enclosures include the kernel transform, local products, derivative-window factors, and subtraction.

6. For each query/particle pair and particle pair, use certified representatives $t_a,t_b\in[0,1)^3$. If $|A(t_a-t_b+\ell)|\le R$, then $|\ell|\le\|A^{-1}\|_2R+\sqrt3$. Compute an outward upper bound $B_R$ for the right-hand side, set $N_R=\lceil B_R\rceil$, and for each required query or particle pair enumerate every integer index in $[-N_R,N_R]^3$. For each candidate compute an outward interval $[r^-,r^+]$ for its image distance and an interval $[R^-,R^+]$ for $R$; include the image if $r^+\le R^-$, exclude it if $r^->R^+$, and return `cutoff-inconclusive` otherwise. Use these finite lists to compute the real potential when requested, real energy, and real force, excluding exactly the own zero-image term $(j,\ell)=(i,0)$ from energy and force before any singular kernel division. For every other retained image certify a positive lower distance bound before dividing; otherwise return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Keep the force convention as the finite sum of differentiated retained pair kernels; do not differentiate the hard-cutoff membership indicator. Add the ordinary Ewald energy constant $-\alpha\sum_iq_i^2/\sqrt\pi$ to the total energy. The point-source potential is only returned off all source images.

7. Compute $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$ and $M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$; if either floor is not determined by its certified enclosure, return `cutoff-inconclusive`. Construct finite $U_3$ real and reciprocal shell controllers with the supplied $J_R,J_K$. For each retained mode, compute outward bounds for $A_k$ and $B_k$ by summing the source/derivative alias terms through $|n_r|\le J_A$ and adding the supplier's finite p-series remainders; for $P=2$, use its finite derivative-window controller. Use $H_k=0$ for the declared analytic-window gather in both force branches; place all finite arithmetic errors in the supplied radii $\varepsilon_{F,i}$. Include every omitted mode in $\mathcal M_{K_c}$ and the mesh-self correction if enabled. Add the actual outward arithmetic radii for all spread, transform, solve, gather, summation, and correction nodes. The outward enclosures for finite controllers themselves use the bounded enclosure interface above; its name does not authorize an unbounded oracle or refinement search. If a required arithmetic radius or controller enclosure is unavailable, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Otherwise retain the computed intervals and total error radii for the final output. Use the same bounded interface for tolerance comparisons: return `certified` when every requested radius is certified to meet its tolerance, `certified-over-tolerance` when at least one is certified to exceed it, and `arithmetic-inconclusive` if neither decision is certified. The total-certificate theorem proves the error bounds and formal operation-count properties for this evaluation; operation counts do not certify accuracy.

## Definition

Inputs are an integer order $n\ge0$, a target $J$ or scaled $I$, an exact
dyadic real argument $x$, positive rational absolute tolerance
$\varepsilon_a$, optional positive rational relative tolerance
$\varepsilon_r$, a fixed exponent range $(e_{\min},e_{\max})$, and finite
positive integer caps $S_{\max},K_{\max},M_{\max},N_{\max},p_{\max},W$, with
$p_{\max}\ge2$.
The caps bound stages, series terms, midpoint panels, Miller terminal index,
dyadic precision, and exact interval operations and subroutine calls. Run
stages $q=1,\ldots,\min(S_{\max},K_{\max},M_{\max},p_{\max})$, using precision
$p=\max(2,\min(q,p_{\max}))$ and elementary-range truncation $q$. Reject
$n<0$, invalid targets, nonpositive tolerances, invalid caps,
$e_{\min}>e_{\max}$, or $x<0$ for the scaled $I$ target with
domain. The scaled
target is always $e^{-x}I_n(x)$.

Use exact rational endpoint formulas for finite sums, recurrences, mesh
construction, and error bounds, with final endpoints rounded outward to
precision $p$. Charge every exact arithmetic operation, range-evaluator
node operation, term, rounding, and loop update to the shared counter $W$;
interrupt a nested elementary-range call with inconclusive before its next
operation would exceed the remaining budget. Factorials use
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. Call
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] for the real sine, cosine, and
exponential ranges in the midpoint branches. Before each call, round its
rational input interval outward to the fixed dyadic format. Its finite outputs are sound by
[[thm-real-elementary-range-enclosures]]. Count each exact operation, term,
rounding, and subroutine call against $W$; if the next operation would
exceed $W$, return inconclusive. A non-finite elementary call makes that
branch unavailable. Final endpoint overflow returns range.

Before forming any stage constant, if the target is scaled $I$ and $x=0$,
use precision $p=p_{\max}$, form $[1,1]$ when $n=0$ and $[0,0]$ when $n\ge1$, and round its
endpoints outward to that format. If either conversion overflows,
return range. Otherwise apply the ordinary absolute-radius test to the rounded candidate and return `success` only when it passes; return `inconclusive` if it fails. The internal exact candidate has radius zero, but outward underflow may widen its stored enclosure. Set a successful output's relative flag by the usual contract test, so a zero value
receives no relative certificate. This branch does not call the
elementary-range procedure.

At stage $q$, compute an outward dyadic interval $P_q$ containing $\pi$
from the Machin identity and alternating arctangent tails in
[[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]]: for
$r=1/5,1/239$, use the $q$-term sum
$\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}(-1)^kr^{2k+1}/(2k+1)$ and tail bound
$r^{2q+1}/((2q+1)(1-r^2))$, combine by $16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)$,
and round outward to the selected format at precision $p$. If this
conversion is non-finite or $\inf P_q\le0$, midpoint candidates are
unavailable at this stage; the independent power-series or Miller branches may
still be attempted.

For a requested $J_n(x)$, first form a power-series candidate if possible.
For any order $r\ge0$, define the finite subroutine $\operatorname{SeriesJ}(r)$:
start
$a_0=(x/2)^r/(0!\,r!)$ and
$a_{k+1}=-a_kx^2/(4(k+1)(k+r+1))$; sum $a_0,\ldots,a_{q-1}$, and
compute $a_q$. Put
$$\rho_J=\frac{x^2}{4(q+1)(q+r+1)}.$$
If $\rho_J<1$, return the interval partial sum enlarged by
$|a_q|/(1-\rho_J)$; otherwise mark this series candidate unavailable.
The tail lemma [[lem-integer-order-bessel-series-tail]] proves each returned
interval contains $J_r(x)$.

For each requested target, also form its composite-midpoint candidate with
$m=q$ panels, $h=\pi/m$, and nodes $\theta_j=(j+\tfrac12)h$,
$j=0,\ldots,m-1$, using $P_q$ as the interval for $\pi$. For $J_n$,
call the elementary-range algorithm for $\sin(\theta_j)$, form
$n\theta_j-x\sin(\theta_j)$, and call it for the cosine of that interval.
Let $Q_m$ be the interval sum $h\sum_j\cos(n\theta_j-x\sin\theta_j)$ and
$$E_J=\frac{h_{\max}^2}{24}\bigl((n+|x|)^2+|x|\bigr), \qquad h_{\max}=\sup(P_q)/m.$$
The candidate is $Q_m/P_q+[-E_J,E_J]$.
For the scaled $I$ target with $x>0$, call the elementary algorithm for
$\cos(\theta_j)$, form
$-x(1-\cos(\theta_j))$, call it for the real exponential, and also call it
for $\cos(n\theta_j)$. Let $Q_m$ be $h$ times the sum of the resulting
product intervals and set
$$E_I=\frac{h_{\max}^2}{24}\bigl((x+n)^2+x\bigr).$$
The candidate is $Q_m/P_q+[-E_I,E_I]$. The exact midpoint error lemmas
[[lem-bessel-integral-midpoint-error]] and
[[lem-scaled-modified-bessel-midpoint-error]] prove these inclusions.

For a $J_n(x)$ Miller candidate, only try this branch when $x>0$ and
$N=n+q\le N_{\max}$. Obtain $\operatorname{SeriesJ}(r)$ for
$r=0,1,n,N+1$; if any is unavailable, skip the branch. Set
$D_0=-J_1$, $D_1=J_0$, and compute
$D_{j+1}=2jD_j/x-D_{j-1}$ for $j=1,\ldots,N$ by interval arithmetic.
Set $u_{N+1}=0,u_N=1$, and compute
$u_{j-1}=2ju_j/x-u_{j+1}$ for $j=N,\ldots,1$. Require the intervals for
$D_{N+1}$, $u_s$, $J_s$, and $J_s+q_MD_s$ below to exclude zero. Form
$q_M=-J_{N+1}/D_{N+1}$. In the fixed order $s=0,1$, whenever the tests
pass, form
$$\widehat J_n=\frac{J_su_n}{u_s},\qquad E_M=\frac{q_M(J_sD_n-J_nD_s)}{J_s+q_MD_s}, \qquad C_M=\widehat J_n-E_M.$$
The exact finite terminal-contamination identity
[[lem-finite-miller-terminal-error-identity]] proves that each $C_M$
contains $J_n(x)$. The Casoratian lemma
[[lem-bessel-casoratian-invariant-positive]] supplies the independent
recurrence pair and positive invariant required by that identity.

Collect every available sound candidate for the requested target. If more
than one is available, intersect them; if the intersection is empty, discard
this stage. Round the selected candidate outward to precision $p$. Return
success at the first stage whose radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. Set
relative_certified to true exactly when relative tolerance was requested,
zero is excluded, and the contract's relative-radius test passes; failure of
that relative test does not prevent absolute success. If no stage succeeds
before the finite caps, return inconclusive. No branch uses a limit in the
Miller terminal index.

## Statement

Let $f:G\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^3$, let $\bar u\in G$, and suppose on an open
neighborhood $N$ of $\bar u$ the system is strictly hyperbolic and each
characteristic field is either genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate. Then
there are $\delta,\eta>0$ such that, whenever
$\|u_L-\bar u\|_2<\delta$ and $\|u_R-\bar u\|_2<\delta$, there is a unique
strength vector $\sigma\in(-\eta,\eta)^m$ satisfying
$$u_R=\Psi_m(\sigma_m;\Psi_{m-1}(\sigma_{m-1};\cdots\Psi_1(\sigma_1;u_L)\cdots)).$$
For the Riemann initial datum $u_0(x)=u_L$ for $x<0$ and $u_R$ for $x>0$,
the corresponding ordered superposition, with waves in increasing family
order, is a self-similar weak solution, meaning it has the form
$u(t,x)=q(x/t)$ for $t>0$. Its nonzero
genuinely nonlinear waves are rarefactions when $\sigma_iD\lambda_i r_i>0$
and strict Lax shocks when $\sigma_iD\lambda_i r_i<0$; its linearly-degenerate
waves are contacts. The neighborhoods are local to $f,N,\bar u$; no arbitrary
large-data solution or uniqueness among all weak solutions is asserted.

## Statement

Fix the finite SBP grid of [[def-periodic-sbp-compressible-viscous-scheme]] and its semidiscrete vector field $L_h$. Let $T>0$, let $\mathcal C\Subset\mathcal G$ be compact, and suppose the exact semidiscrete solution $\bar U:[0,T]\to\mathcal G^{|\mathcal I|}$ starts from $U^0$ and satisfies $\bar U_i(t)\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal C$ for every node and every $t\in[0,T]$. For any finite step count $N\ge1$ with $N\Delta t\le T$, the guarded algorithm [[alg-positive-tube-forward-euler-for-compressible-sbp]] completes all $N$ steps for sufficiently small $\Delta t$, and

$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|U^n-\bar U(n\Delta t)\|\le C_{h,T}\Delta t.$$

Here the norm is Euclidean on the finite nodal state vector. The constant may depend on the fixed grid, coefficient parameters, tube, and exact trajectory; no mesh-uniform estimate is asserted.

## Statement

Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, maximum diameter $h\to0$, and mesh-aligned material interfaces. Let $\epsilon,\mu$ be time-independent symmetric uniformly positive definite bounded coefficients. Let $(E,B)$ be a PEC solution of [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] with $J_{\rm src}\in C^1([0,T];L^2(\Omega)^3)$, satisfying the stated current continuity and magnetic divergence constraints. Assume $E,E_t,E_{tt}$ are piecewise $C^1$ in space, their curls are piecewise $C^1$, and their tangential traces match across interior mesh faces and vanish on the exterior PEC boundary; assume $B(0)$ is piecewise $C^1$ with matching normal traces and $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$. These bounds are uniform in time on $[0,T]$.

Take the semidiscrete solution of [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]] with exact load moments, initialize $E_h(0)=R_hE(0)$ using the Maxwell Ritz map of [[def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection]], and initialize $B_h(0)=B_h^0$ by [[lem-maxwell-magnetic-compatible-initial-projection]]. Write $\theta_h(t)=E_h(t)-R_hE(t)$. The Countable Choice assumption required by that projection interface is in force. Then the semidiscrete solution exists uniquely and
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left(\|E_h(t)-E(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(E_h(t)-E(t))\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|B_h(t)-B(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\right)\le C_T h.$$
The constant depends on $T$, the coefficient bounds, the shape-regularity and projection bounds, and the stated piecewise smooth norms, but not on $h$. The initial magnetic projection preserves the discrete divergence constraint, and its error $B_h^0-B(0)$ is $\mu^{-1}$-orthogonal to all discrete curls. The result is a PEC semidiscrete estimate for smooth mesh-aligned data; it does not claim a rate across unresolved jumps or for nonsmooth fields.

## Statement

Every invocation of [[alg-finite-gaussian-basis-integral-recurrence-evaluation]] terminates after finitely many operations bounded by its work and child-evaluator caps. If it returns `success`, each integral interval contains the exact integral range over the supplied parameter boxes. For the real energy/gradient branch, the returned energy interval and gradient-error bound contain the corresponding values of the finite functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]]. The reported discarded-energy bound is at least the sum of the absolute Cauchy–Schwarz bounds for all skipped terms. The evaluator may return `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; no universal success or exact-sparsity claim is made.

## Definition

**Inputs.** A finite list of input basis contractions $\phi_a=\sum_{i=1}^{q_a}d_{ai}g_{ai}$, $1\le a\le n$, from [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], represented by finite dyadic intervals for real centers and positive exponents and finite dyadic intervals or complex rectangles for coefficients; a finite nuclear list; positive integral and energy tolerances for the requested outputs; an optional positive gradient tolerance, defaulting to the energy tolerance when absent; optional positive screening tolerance; finite positive integer work and precision caps $W,P$; and a dyadic format of precision $2\le p\le P$ with exponent bounds and fixed elementary truncation index $K\ge1$. A primitive request is the singleton-contraction case. An energy/gradient request additionally requires $n,r\ge1$, real basis coefficients, real nuclear data, real matrices $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ given by dyadic boxes (exact matrices are singleton boxes), and uniform finite bounds $B\ge\sup\|C\|_F$, $M_D\ge\sup\|D\|_F$ from [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]]. Internal primitive labels $(a,i)$ are distinct from the input basis labels $a$; $C$ is a subsequent transform of the input basis.

**Outputs.** A status `success`, `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; outward real intervals or complex rectangles for the requested overlap, kinetic, nuclear-attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals; when requested, an energy interval, a gradient center and a Frobenius gradient-error bound; and a separately accumulated discarded-energy bound. Success encloses every parameter value in the input boxes. No status declares an omitted integral zero.

**Finite calls and accounting.** Use [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] for arithmetic. Every real elementary call means a typed DAG call to [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] at the supplied format and $K$. Enclose $\pi$ by the $K$-term Machin/arctangent certificate in [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]], with exact rational tail endpoints before final outward conversion. A shared counter charges each conversion, comparison, loop update, arithmetic operation, recurrence update and summand, including every primitive operation executed by a child. Check the counter before executing an operation and interrupt any child at exhaustion. A required Boys call receives remaining work $R$ as its finite work cap, precision cap $P$, the same format and $K$, absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_I/2$ where $\varepsilon_I$ is the integral tolerance, and no relative request; its actual work is charged to the parent. A required child non-success propagates its status, except that a rounded intermediate failing a domain certification on valid original data yields `inconclusive`. Overflow yields `range`; cap exhaustion yields `inconclusive`. These choices are conservative and need not permit success under every cap or tolerance.

1. Validate positive exponent lower endpoints, finite input boxes, indices in $\mathbb N_0^3$, supported format and positive tolerances/caps. Invalid original data return `domain`. For energy/gradient verify realness and dimensions and certify the norm bounds by outward Frobenius upper bounds on the complete boxes. If this sufficient norm test cannot certify the supplied bounds, return `inconclusive`; do not claim that an unknown represented matrix violates its bound. Form finite requested primitive-pair and quartet lists lexicographically. Include all shifted overlap pairs required by the kinetic raising/lowering formula; a negative index contributes zero.

2. For each ordered primitive pair with exponents $a,b$, indices $\alpha,\beta$ and centers $A,B$, compute $p=a+b$, $P=(aA+bB)/p$, and $K_{ab}=\exp(-ab\|A-B\|^2/p)$ by outward arithmetic and the real elementary call. Compute the Hermite coefficients by [[thm-cartesian-pair-hermite-expansion-and-coefficient-recurrence]], raising the first primitive in x,y,z order and then the second, storing each intermediate degree table until its successors have been formed. The final table has $\prod_{j=1}^3(\alpha_j+\beta_j+1)$ entries; every intermediate table update is also charged. Compute overlap by the finite shifted polynomial expansion and the moments in [[lem-cartesian-gaussian-moments-and-parameter-derivatives]], and kinetic by [[thm-cartesian-gaussian-raising-lowering-and-kinetic-recurrences]]. Certified square roots and integer powers evaluate all half-integer factors in those moment formulas.

3. To evaluate an attraction primitive pair, put $L=|\alpha|+|\beta|$ and use exponent $\eta=p$ and center difference $P-C_{\rm nuc}$. To evaluate a primitive Coulomb quartet, including any diagonal self quartet, put $L=|\alpha|+|\beta|+|\gamma|+|\delta|$, $\eta=pq/(p+q)$ and center difference $P-Q$, where the second pair has exponent $q$. Form the nonnegative Boys argument interval $\mathcal T=\eta\|P-Q\|^2$, with the evident attraction substitution, using interval squaring and the positive exponent bounds. Request Boys orders $0,\ldots,L$ from [[alg-certified-boys-finite-budget-branch-evaluation]]. If rounding prevents certification of a required positive denominator, return `inconclusive`.

4. Initialize $R^j_{000}=(-2\eta)^jF_j(\mathcal T)$ for $0\le j\le L$. For total derivative degree $d=1,\ldots,L$, enumerate $(t,u,v)$ lexicographically with $t+u+v=d$, choose its first nonzero coordinate in x,y,z order, and apply that coordinate's recurrence in [[thm-gaussian-coulomb-hermite-recurrences-and-integral-formulas]] for $0\le j\le L-d$. Negative-index terms are zero. For example, when $t>0$, use $R^j_{tuv}=(P_1-Q_1)R^{j+1}_{t-1,u,v}+(t-1)R^{j+1}_{t-2,u,v}$. Each predecessor is at a smaller derivative degree and within its stored Boys-order range. Contract the finite Hermite sums in that theorem to get each primitive integral.

5. Contract primitive integrals to input-basis integrals by the finite coefficient sums. For overlap, kinetic and attraction the coefficient is $\overline{d_{ai}}d_{bj}$. For the defined pair-density Coulomb convention, the primitive quartet coefficient is $d_{ai}\overline{d_{bj}}\overline{d_{ck}}d_{dl}$: expand $\overline{f_{ab}(x)}f_{cd}(y)$ in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]]. In the real energy branch these are the four real contraction coefficients. Cache only identical ordered parameter boxes, angular indices, format and truncation context; an $R$ cache record also stores its cutoff $L$. Reuse a table only if its stored cutoff is at least the needed cutoff; otherwise compute the larger table under the counter.

6. Optional Coulomb-energy screening applies to whole input-basis quartets, before their off-diagonal primitive quartets are evaluated. First compute every required contracted diagonal $G_{ab,ab}$ without screening by steps 2–5, including all coefficients $d$. Obtain finite nonnegative upper endpoints $U_{ab}$ from their real projections, justified by [[thm-positive-coulomb-bilinear-cauchy-schwarz-screening]]. Form the outward real interval $W_{ab}=\sum_{p,q}C_{ap}D_{pq}C_{bq}$ and its upper absolute bound $A_{ab}=\max(|\inf W_{ab}|,|\sup W_{ab}|)$. Compute nonnegative outward upper bounds $Q_{abcd}\ge\sqrt{U_{ab}U_{cd}}$ and $w_{abcd}\ge\tfrac12A_{ab}A_{cd}Q_{abcd}$. Enumerate all ordered candidate basis quartets lexicographically, with no unrecorded symmetry compression. Skip a quartet only if the outward accumulated sum after adding $w_{abcd}$ is at most the screening tolerance; otherwise compute its primitive sums. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral $D$ in dimension two or three, and a shape-regular conforming mesh. Let $C_I$ be the mesh-independent constant in the RT0 interpolation estimate and let $L$ be a coordinate-slab width for $D$. If $B_D$ is the actual right inverse of [[thm-na-bounded-lipschitz-domain-divergence-right-inverse]], define
$$S_hq_h:=I_hB_Dq_h,\qquad C_R:=C_I C_{\rm div}(L+\operatorname{diam}D).$$
Then $S_h:Q_h\to V_h$ is a linear right inverse of divergence and $\|S_hq_h\|_{L^2(D)}\le C_R\|q_h\|_{L^2(D)}$. Consequently $\|S_hq_h\|_{H(\operatorname{div})}\le\sqrt{1+C_R^2}\|q_h\|_2$. When $Q_h\ne\{0\}$, the RT0/P0 inf-sup constant satisfies $\beta_h\ge(1+C_R^2)^{-1/2}$ uniformly in mesh size.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the real trial/test spaces and bilinear form of [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]], with $|b(w,v)|\le5\|w\|_U\|v\|_V$ as in [[lem-na-ultraweak-poisson-bilinear-form-bounded]]. The ideal trial-to-test map $T$ of [[alg-na-ultraweak-poisson-ideal-trial-to-test]] is well defined, bounded linear, and satisfies $\|T\|\le5$. Let $x\in U$ be any exact ultraweak solution and let $U_h\subset U$ be finite dimensional. The ideal DPG equations with test space $T(U_h)$ have a unique solution $x_h$, which is the orthogonal projection of $x$ in the induced energy inner product $(w,z)_E=(Tw,Tz)_V$. Consequently $\|x-x_h\|_E=\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_E=\|B(x-x_h)\|_{V'}$.

The ideal trial-to-test map $T$ of [[alg-na-ultraweak-poisson-ideal-trial-to-test]] is well defined, bounded linear, and satisfies $\|T\|\le5$. Let $x\in U$ be any exact ultraweak solution and let $U_h\subset U$ be finite dimensional. The ideal DPG equations with test space $T(U_h)$ have a unique solution $x_h$, which is the orthogonal projection of $x$ in the induced energy inner product $(w,z)_E=(Tw,Tz)_V$. Consequently $\|x-x_h\|_E=\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_E=\|B(x-x_h)\|_{V'}$.

## Example

Use Euclidean norm on $X=\mathbb R^2$ and exact matrix/load
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad f=\binom10.$$
Approximate it by
$$\widetilde A=A+E,\qquad E=\begin{pmatrix}1/100&0\\0&-1/100\end{pmatrix},\qquad \widetilde f=f.$$
The exact coercivity and continuity constants are $c=1$ and $C=3$. The defect matrix is $E=\operatorname{diag}(1/100,-1/100)$, so $\|E\|_2=1/100<1/50$; take the conservative certified $\delta=1/50$, load defect $\eta=0$, and $\|F_h\|=1$. The perturbed solve is
$$\widetilde u=\binom{19900/29999}{-10000/29999},$$
while $u=(2/3,-1/3)$. The transfer theorem gives the certified error $\|u-\widetilde u\|_2\le1/49$; the exact rational difference is also smaller than $1/49$.

This is a finite algebraic error ledger illustrating how a certified assembly defect enters the perturbation theorem; it does not assert that this particular matrix is a panel matrix from a specified mesh.

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be any bounded connected Lipschitz polygon, including polygons with holes, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be any finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh. Use the exact two-dimensional P1/R3 practical family selected in PE30: volume fields $\sigma_h|_K\in P_1(K)^2$ and $u_h|_K\in P_1(K)$; compatible global scalar traces of degree at most two on facets, zero on boundary facets; conservative global normal traces of degree at most one; and broken tests $V_r=\prod_K(P_3(K)^2\times P_3(K))$, with the graph inner product inherited from $V$. The local Fortin projection $\Pi:V\to V_r$ is that of [[lem-na-practical-dpg-fortin-p1-r3]], and $C_\Pi$ is its operator norm bound. For each $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, the continuous ultraweak solution $x$ and practical solution $x_h$ exist uniquely, with $$\|x-x_h\|_U\le(1+5C_\Pi C_*)\inf_{z_h\in U_h}\|x-z_h\|_U.$$ For every $\widetilde x_h\in U_h$, put $\eta=\|F_f-B\widetilde x_h\|_{V_r'}$, where $V_r'$ is the dual of $V_r$ with its induced norm, and $\operatorname{osc}(F_f)=\|F_f\circ(I-\Pi)\|_{V'}$. Then $$C_*^{-2}\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U^2\le\eta^2+(C_\Pi\eta+\operatorname{osc}(F_f))^2,\qquad \eta\le5\|x-\widetilde x_h\|_U,$$ and $$\operatorname{osc}(F_f)\le C_{\rm osc}\left(\sum_Kh_K^2\|f-f_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad f_K=|K|^{-1}\int_Kf,$$ where $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and $C_{\rm osc}$ is the cellwise constant from the Fortin map's mean-preserving local $L^2$ estimate. The constants $C_*$, $C_\Pi$, and $C_{\rm osc}$ are independent of mesh size for the fixed domain and shape-regular family. The practical corollary is two-dimensional; the continuous graph theorem also covers dimension three.
